detail.abstract:
The 2026 Prize in Economic Sciences recognised Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for the
microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation. This article asks what their
framework implies for artificial intelligence (AI) in the ten largest economies by 2026 nominal
GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026): the United States, China, Germany, Japan,
the United Kingdom, India, France, Russia, Italy and Brazil. I build a country index of
occupational AI exposure from ILOSTAT employment by ISCO-08 major group and the AI
Occupational Exposure scores of Felten, Raj and Seamans, and combine it with Stanford HAI
capacity data, the IMF AI Preparedness Index, IMF fiscal data and BIS policy rates. Three findings
emerge. First, AI capacity is far more concentrated than output: the United States and China
produce 64% of the group's GDP but account for 90% of its AI private investment, and
occupational exposure is unrelated to AI capacity (Spearman ρ = 0.02, exact permutation p =
0.97). Second, two pre-specified hypotheses are not supported: the most exposed economies do
not have systematically less fiscal or monetary space (ρ = 0.14, p = 0.71), and lagged AI
investment does not predict labour-productivity growth in 2018–2025 (randomisation p = 0.86).
Third, a calibrated exercise based on the consumption Euler equation shows that, when the
intertemporal elasticity of substitution is below one, an AI-driven rise in trend growth raises the
interest–growth differential. With an elasticity of 0.5 and the mid-range OECD productivity
scenario, the debt-stabilising primary balance rises by 1.1 percentage points of GDP in Japan and
by 0.7–0.8 points in the United States, Italy and France. The gain would widen monetary room
above the lower bound while narrowing fiscal room where public debt is highest.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly relevant to fleet maintenance, customer service, and sustainability management, yet these functions are often examined as separate areas of organizational innovation. In U.S. car-rental operations, their interdependence creates a managerial challenge: maintenance requirements, uncertain vehicle return times, reservation commitments, and environmental objectives compete for the same limited fleet resources. This article aims to identify the organizational and managerial capabilities required to coordinate AI-enabled predictive maintenance, customer service analytics, and sustainability analytics within an integrated operational framework. The proposed study adopts a structured literature synthesis, drawing on the supplied scholarly literature, additional verifiable peer-reviewed research, relevant industry reports, and authoritative transportation and environmental datasets where available. The synthesis will examine data integration, cross-functional governance, managerial decision-making, workforce analytical literacy, operational flexibility, organizational learning, and sustainability measurement. It will distinguish direct evidence from findings transferred from adjacent sectors and identify methodological limitations and unresolved questions. The intended contribution is an evidence-grounded conceptual framework linking technological foundations and organizational capabilities to coordinated AI-supported decisions and operational, customer, and environmental outcomes. The framework will also generate testable propositions and candidate performance indicators for future empirical investigation. Ultimately, the study seeks to clarify how organizational implementation, accountable decision-making, and measurable outcomes can shape the value of AI integration in car-rental operations. Its conclusions will be finalized after the literature search and synthesis are completed.

title: Who Pays for Saying That 'Winter Is Coming'? Reviewing A Clinician's Departure from a Rule Under Deep Uncertainty: A Conceptual Analysis

detail.abstract:
In 2003, an emergency physician in Toronto asked on 9, 16 and 18 May for a SARS unit for one family. Each request was refused, and the four patients were later classed as SARS cases. The SARS Commission that reviewed the case knew how it ended; the clinicians did not. Rules cut noise by making clinicians decide alike but can misclassify edge cases. Any clinician who spots one faces the Toronto physician's choice: keep to the rule or depart. Just Culture asks who draws the line between tolerable and culpable acts. It leaves open how to judge a decision taken when the futures could be listed but not ranked.

By mid-May, Toronto was told SARS was over. A physician who said 'Winter is coming' and was wrong would have been blamed for a false alarm, and the next clinician would have kept quiet. We extend Dekker's account of who draws the line with an earlier question: could anyone then have ranked the futures? On 9 May, nobody could rank SARS above a widow's pneumonia, and a review that reads only the notes written then can defend both the request and the refusal. Whatever staff tell a separate learning track stays there, and the medical director accepts the price: a real failing may go unproved. The Commission found that the front-line warnings "went into a black hole". The lesson that travels is a channel past the gatekeeper, and reviews built this way should leave more objections on paper.

detail.abstract: Small home-services firms are told to pick a few channels and do them well. This article names, defines and tests an alternative, the Everything Affects Everything (EAE) principle: a firm's channels are read together as one record, so the return to any channel depends on the others. The study measured eight public channels for 835 heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) contractors in ten US metropolitan areas and related them to whether four generative AI assistants recommended each firm. The strong form of EAE failed. A weakest-link model fitted worst, an additive model best, and no channel pair showed significant synergy. A refined, exploratory form fitted. Necessary condition analysis identified Google Business Profile and reviews as gates under every treatment of missing data, and a basic website as a third when unreadable sites were excluded. None of the 72 firms with ten or more mentions was weak in any gate. Beyond the gates, breadth was associated with recommendation: among gate-passing firms, 28% with no other strong channel were recommended, against 64% with all five others. EAE is restated as a gated, cumulative system, giving small firms a sequence: secure the gates, then widen.

However, its planned withdrawal from China also highlights the risks of international expansion and the need to reassess market performance. The study concludes that URC’s internationalization strategy demonstrates the value of glocalization, combining standardized operational capabilities with localized products, pricing, promotions, and distribution. Its experience offers practical lessons for Philippine businesses seeking international growth through market research, appropriate entry strategies, and continuous evaluation of foreign market performance.

detail.abstract:
What does society gain and lose when states reduce criminal penalties for drug pos-
session? Using FBI arrest and crime records and CDC death records, I compare Oregon’s and
Washington’s 2021 reforms with weighted comparison states that tracked them before 2021. Drug-
user arrests fall 68 percent with no shift to other charges, while overdose deaths rise 34 percent and
property crime 17 percent. Deaths rise in every comparison group, including groups matched on
COVID, fentanyl’s spread and state politics. Restoring penalties in Washington brings arrests back
but not deaths down. Health and crime costs outweigh the gains from less enforcement: a net social
cost of $26.6 billion by mid-2023, mostly from 1,971 excess deaths. The results show that reducing
penalties for drug possession can cut arrests sharply and still leave society worse off.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a test of private values (PV) against common values (CV) for repeated auctions using a field experiment that induces exogenous variation in submitted bids. Existing empirical approaches often require bidder participation data; this test uses only a bidder's own bids, wins, payments, and ex-post outcomes, and it can be run by individual market participants. Raising a bid mechanically expands the set of auctions a bidder can win to include marginal auctions with higher rival bids. Under PV, these higher bids contain no information about value conditional on the bidder's own information, but under CV they do. In partnership with an ad management platform in Brazil, I apply the test to online display advertising auctions. The findings provide empirical support for the PV assumption commonly maintained but not directly tested in quantitative models of this literature.

detail.abstract:
Background: Violence against children is a pervasive violation of human rights with lasting public health, social, and economic repercussions. While extensive research has documented health consequences of childhood violence in Mexico and globally, the long-term economic impact remains underexplored, particularly on women’s educational attainment and labour income.

Methods: We use data from Mexico’s 2021 National Survey on the Dynamics of Relationships in Households (ENDIREH) to estimate the effects of violence experienced by women in childhood (exposure to sexual, physical, or emotional abuse before age 15) on their educational attainment and adult wages and calculate aggregate and lifetime productivity losses to estimate the macroeconomic impact of childhood violence. To address the endogeneity of education and selection bias in labour market participation, we use a natural experiment from a 1992 education reform and a two-step Heckman correction model. 

Findings: Among 110,127 women surveyed, 43% reported experiencing childhood violence. Exposure to childhood violence reduced respondents’ formal education by 0.28 years of schooling (95% CI: –0.32 to –0.24) and was associated with a 7% wage penalty independent of level of education (95% CI: –9% to –5%). We estimate that 8.3 million economically active women in Mexico have experienced childhood violence with associated annual productivity losses of US$5.3 billion (9% of total labour income of the survivors). Cumulative lifetime losses are projected at US$135 billion in present value terms, equivalent to approximately 7.5% of Mexico’s 2024 GDP.

Interpretation:The economic, as well as the health, burden of childhood violence in Mexico is substantial and it constitutes a structural determinant of human capital formation and national economic performance. Violence experienced in childhood undermines women’s educational attainment and lifetime labour income, resulting in substantial individual and macroeconomic costs. Addressing childhood violence must become core to strategies for reducing poverty, advancing gender equity and improving productivity and hence to fulfilling the Sustainable Development Goals. We call for urgent, coordinated investment in prevention, survivor support, and legal protections to break cycles of violence and secure inclusive growth.

detail.abstract: Can artificial intelligence offset the economic cost of population ageing? We estimate a panelVARX on annual data for 28 Eastern European and Central Asian economies over nearly threedecades, tracing how demographic change shapes growth, investment, saving, real interest rates, and labour-force participation. AI enters the counterfactuals as an exogenous productivity shock, calibrated to recent US estimates and scaled by each country’s AI preparedness. Population ageing lowers projected per-capita growth across the region over the next two decades. The drag is largest in the EU-11 member states, followed by Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Across the region it amounts to about one percentage point of per capita growth between 2025 and 2045, and slightly more, 1.04 percentage points, in the EU-11, where endogenous capital deepening then absorbs a little over half of it. How far AI can ease these headwinds depends more on the size of the productivity gains than on preparedness. Summed over 2026–2045, modest gains offset about 15 per cent of the demographic drag in each region, while optimistic gains offset all of it in the regional averages, though not in several rapidly ageing Eastern European and Western Balkan economies. The relief lasts only as long as the adoption wave. Central Asian countries, still young, have a window to invest in digital infrastructure, human capital, and regulation before ageing intensifies.

detail.abstract: This paper integrates a research programme whose central premise is that productivity can be promoted from the level of individual psychology. Drawing on the happy-productive worker thesis, broaden-and-build theory, conservation of resources theory and the distinction between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, it argues that well-being operates as a resource that is converted into performance through experiential engagement, and that this conversion is shaped by organisational and structural conditions. The paper maps the author's published and in-progress work onto three levels (individual psychological resources, organisational and relational conditions, and structural context), supported by an enabling layer of transparent methods and research ethics. From this mapping it derives six propositions and a research agenda that emphasises longitudinal and quasiexperimental designs, multilevel and measurement-invariance testing, and the explicit study of boundary conditions, including the possible costs of flow and eudaimonic striving. The paper is conceptual: it reports no new empirical results, and unpublished manuscripts are described by topic and status only. It closes by discussing the limits of the programme, notably its reliance on selfreported, largely cross-sectional data from Mexico and Latin America, and by stating an ethical caveat: promoting well-being for the sake of productivity must not reduce workers to inputs.

detail.abstract:
Researchers have long studied how companies use psychological principles to sell, but social media has made these techniques cheaper to use and harder to notice. This paper draws on self-discrepancy theory, psychologist E. Tory Higgins' idea that people experience distress over the gap between the "actual self" and the "ideal self" or "ought self," to argue that many of today's highest-performing ads sell a promise of the "ideal self." This paper surveys existing literature on self-discrepancy theory and the history of persuasive mechanisms in advertising, identifying self-discrepancy as a prominent device, one which I hypothesize is exacerbated by targeted social media ads. 

This study conducts a pilot analysis of 14 randomly selected top-performing online video ads from large brands advertising in the United States. Using a list of persuasion techniques drawn from prior research, it finds that eight of the 14 ads explicitly opened a gap between the viewer's actual and ideal or ought self, and those eight used an average of 5.3 other persuasion techniques, compared with 1.5 in the remaining six. This study also includes original interviews with senior marketing executives at Delta Air Lines, AT&T, and a large telecommunications company, and finds that none of the three reported measuring whether its marketing leaves customers better off in the long term. 

The paper proposes a persuasion "sweet spot" defined by three tests: understanding, gap, and aftermath. It recommends that firms track regret, satisfaction, and repurchase through a follow-up survey linked to the ad that produced each sale. If adopted by companies, this solution could be mutually beneficial: customers get products that serve goals they already have, and companies gain a more loyal customer base.

AI disclosure: AI tools assisted with ad transcription and preliminary coding; all codes were reviewed by the author.

detail.abstract: As digital technologies become more deeply integrated into everyday life, they may shape fertility through competing channels. On one hand, digital activities can displace face-to-face interaction, offline leisure and family time. On the other hand, digital technologies can increase flexible work arrangements, reduce information costs and ease coordinating family life. Does greater digital life correspond to higher or lower fertility trends, and for whom? I construct a state-year Digital Life Index for the United States that captures three dimensions of digitalization: remote work, digital leisure, and access to internet services. A one-standard-deviation increase in the lagged index is associated with approximately 2.1 fewer births per 1,000 women ages 30-39 years. The estimates for women in their twenties and forties are statistically insignificant. This negative relationship is more pronounced among married women living with their spouses, women in occupations with higher potential for remote work, and women with postsecondary education less than bachelor's degree. Spouse's occupation also plays an important role: the relationship goes in opposite direction depending on whether husbands are in jobs with high potential for remote work or jobs that require face-to-face interaction. The findings suggest that digital life has a negative relationship with fertility trends, but this relationship is heterogeneous by work and family circumstances.

detail.abstract: Women in rural agrarian households are constrained in their ownership of individual assets and their access to financial resources. We test the effects of relaxing households' liquidity constraints through the randomized provision of collateral-free loans to 1,429 farming households across 80 villages. Since Indian farming households rely on joint contributions from men and women, and the loan increased household ownership of goods that benefit both members. We explore its impacts on household members' individual residual income and private consumption. The loan product enhanced women's financial autonomy and uptake of digital financial services, accompanied by an expansion of women's access to resources. Women in households that received the loan allocated more hours to leisure and fewer to farm and non-farm work on the busiest day of the agricultural season than the control group, although women's labor supply across the agricultural season and household farm income did not change between treatment and control villages. The loan did not affect women's intrahousehold bargaining power but amplified pre-existing cooperative household arrangements. The results suggest that credit to households with joint production can improve women's outcomes, such as access to resources and financial inclusion, that are often difficult to affect through targeted resource provision.

detail.title: Dynamic Synthesis of Phase-Space Files for Gantry-Angle Dependent Monte Carlo Dose Calculations in Linac Treatment Planning
detail.abstract: Abstract Over recent decades, Monte Carlo (MC) techniques have seen growing adoption in Medical Linear Accelerator (LinAc) treatment planning, primarily driven by their unparalleled dosimetric precision. Within the LinAc head, the Multileaf Collimator (MLC) is crucial for tailoring the radiation field to conform to the tumor volume, thereby maximizing target dose while shielding adjacent healthy tissues. During static-jaw radiotherapy, the MLC apertures continuously adapt to the rotational trajectory of the gantry, despite the remainder of the accelerator geometry remaining fixed. To streamline treatment planning and bypass the prohibitive computational costs associated with repeated full-system MC modeling, phase-space files (PSFs) are routinely utilized. This work presents and validates a novel computational strategy for synthesizing PSFs situated directly beneath the MLC. Crucially, these synthesized PSFs dynamically morph to reflect the exact beam configuration dictated by the gantry's angular position. The proposed methodology is anchored by an extensive database of pre-computed MC probability distributions. For validation purposes, dosimetric data from a simulated 6 MV LinAc photon beam were utilized. The generated PSFs were rigorously benchmarked against empirical measurements and full-length MC simulations featuring diverse aperture shapes. Ultimately, the analysis demonstrates that organ dose metrics derived from the synthetically generated PSFs exhibit strong statistical equivalence to those produced by reference PSFs. This innovative framework not only introduces a highly efficient mechanism for accelerating LinAc treatment planning workflows but also highlights the broader necessity of high-fidelity dose modeling in clinical radiation therapy.

detail.abstract: In the presence of communication frictions, individuals must draw inferences about the information they receive from others. Building on a simple theoretical model we experimentally investigate strategic information exchange in the presence of costly and coarse communication. While we find support for the model's prediction that individuals respond to the instrumental value of information, there is significant overparticipation in costly information exchange. Moreover, participants fail to account for the strategic behavior of others, in line with the literature on selection neglect and failures of contingent reasoning. Failures occur in both directions, with uninformed agents refusing to use valuable information and well-informed agents blindly "following the crowd". In a subsequent online experiment, we consider potential drivers of the gap between theoretical predictions and experimental results, varying the complexity of the information updating task and introducing a non-social source of additional information. Our results suggest that people fail to use contextual information when interpreting the information they receive from peers, highlighting one way that the "wisdom of the crowd" can fail.

detail.abstract: Using a five-year survey of over 170,000 US consumers, we provide a novel direct measure of attention to monetary policy and show that the data strongly support the predictions of a rational inattention model. First, attention is incentive-driven: consumers with "skin in the game"-those planning major purchases like homes or cars-are significantly more attentive to monetary policy news. Second, attention varies systematically with interest rate volatility and news supply, exhibiting cyclical patterns around FOMC meetings. Third, marginal effects of volatility and news supply decline with "skin in the game," implying external factors primarily affect low-skin-in-the-game consumers. These findings imply that, when communication is costly and attention is endogenous, optimal central bank communications in our model target consumers who bear the largest welfare losses from information frictions. This targeted communication approach increases aggregate attention to monetary policy, leading to an amplified response of consumption to interest rate changes.

detail.abstract: How should the gains from AI be divided among displaced workers, remaining workers, and firms? We study people's fairness preference in preregistered, incentivized spectator experiments with over 4,800 participants in the United States and China. Participants divide real monetary bonuses among the parties to an actual production process. For displaced workers, AI replacement reduces their claims but does not eliminate them. The absence of current work and changes in initial allocations partly explain this reduction, but we find no evidence that AI's superior performance does. Disclosing displaced workers' past contributions to AI training strengthens their claims, whereas reemployment does not weaken them. For remaining workers, they are viewed as deserving gains from both replacement and augmentation. Disclosing past training contributions does not strengthen augmented workers' claims. Beyond the effect of a larger pool, better performance achieved with AI assistance strengthens augmented workers' claims in China but weakens them in the United States. For firms, the extent to which they are viewed as deserving AI gains depends strongly on how those gains are initially assigned.

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between CEO overconfidence and corporate greenwashing. Using a sample of Chinese listed firms, we find that overconfident CEOs choose to greenwash less ex ante.  Firms led by these CEOs tend to generate more patent applications and grants, and these innovation outputs help explain the negative relationship. This relationship is stronger among state-owned enterprises and weaker when the CEO also chairs the board. Lower carbon emissions and CEOs’ business degrees strengthen this relationship, whereas capital intensity and regional economic development do not. Interestingly, however, when overconfident CEOs realize that they have overestimated earnings, they turn to greenwashing ex post. Our findings further highlight the importance of educational backgrounds and attainment in shaping the overconfidence of CEOs which leads to more innovation and less greenwashing (ex ante). The study offers practical implications for regulators and stakeholders assessing greenwashing risk.

detail.abstract: An AI productivity boom can warrant lower nominal rates even when most gains are anticipated. I derive analytical representations of optimal rates under commitment and discretion in an economy with sticky prices and wages and hand-to-mouth households. Holding the realized productivity path fixed, I vary expectations. Anticipated gains raise the natural rate, but below-target inflation supports real wages and keeps nominal rates lower. Surprises leave the natural rate unchanged, calling for cuts. After surprises, expected redistribution toward hand-to-mouth households calls for deeper rate cuts to sustain savers’ spending. Raising rates requires more anticipation when wages are stickier relative to prices.

detail.abstract: A growing number of consumer financial products are offered by outside firms on a bank's charter, through banking-as-a-service arrangements. Banks that rent out their charters this way hold the deposits those firms bring but not the relationship with the depositor. Among 408 relationships between 299 firms and 70 US banks, the rate those banks pay on interest-bearing deposits rises 8% over the four years after their earliest documented rental begins, relative to matched banks, a rise that grows with the federal funds rate. The deposits arrive in smaller accounts; the cash share of assets rises 1.7 percentage points and the loan share falls 2.1. Fee income grows: other noninterest income rises 59%. Return on assets rises at banks renting to two or more firms and not at those renting to one. Insolvency risk grows: the Z-score falls 18% and net charge-offs rise 28%.

detail.abstract: Using institutional holding data for bank holding companies (BHCs) from 2001Q1 through 2024Q2, we examine the role of BHC climate risk on herding by institutional investors (II) and whether herding reflects informed behavior regarding subsequent bank outcomes. Employing buyand sell-side variants of the Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny (LSV) herding measure, we find that buyside herding by dedicated IIs is positively associated with contemporaneous climate risk, suggesting that dedicated IIs may be more willing to engage in herd buying in climate-exposed BHCs, while transient IIs reduce their subsequent buy-side herding against climate exposure of their holdings. We also find that sell-side herding by dedicated IIs of high climate risk BHCs is followed by lower charge-off ratios, consistent with the possibility of market discipline through exit signals. In contrast, buy-side herding of high climate exposure BHCs by transient IIs is associated with lower Tobin's Q, suggesting that herding by short-horizon IIs does not translate into superior valuation outcomes. Finally, buy-side herding by dedicated IIs is followed by greater general climate exposure, driven by opportunity exposure, whereas transient-II buy-side herding is followed by lower opportunity exposure. Our findings suggest that dedicated IIs may be willing to invest collectively in BHCs pursuing climate-related opportunities.

detail.abstract: Broadly diversified equity investments are a suitable building block for the third pillar of retirement provision. Since 1987, Austrian equities have returned 4.46 percent per year in real terms after Austrian tax on investment income (KESt) and before costs, European equities 4.18 percent, and savings invested at the money-market rate (the savings proxy) −0.25 percent. In the sample starting in 1970, no window of 20 years or more ends in a real loss for Austrian equities, compared with more than 40 percent of the twenty-year windows for the savings proxy. The series extended back to 1958 returns 4.07 percent per year in real terms after KESt but also shows seven twenty-year windows that end in a real loss. Austria’s own subsidized product, the Zukunftsvorsorge, combines a mandatory capital guarantee with an equity allocation invested mainly in the home market. Its number of contracts has more than halved since 2012. This purchasing-power analysis for Austrian investors under today’s tax rules, the Austrian experience, and an international comparison of account models yield criteria for an Austrian retirement savings account.

detail.abstract: Retail investors now monitor financial markets through applications that deliver prices, news, and portfolio values continuously throughout the day. This paper addresses a problem created by that access: monitoring itself consumes attention, and attention is a limited cognitive resource that decision making requires. Drawing on prospect theory, research on investor attention, and the distinction between fast intuitive processing and slow deliberative processing, the paper develops an original theoretical model that links notification exposure to checking frequency, checking frequency to perceived stress, stress to impulsive trading, and repeated trading to regret and reduced decision confidence and quality. The model is expressed as five propositions and five directional, testable hypotheses. The paper then specifies a rigorous empirical strategy for testing the model, combining a survey of active retail investors with a 14 day diary and experience sampling component. The contribution is threefold. First, the paper reframes frequent price checking, usually treated as diligence, as a potential cost with measurable consequences. Second, it identifies perceived stress as the central mediating mechanism between monitoring and impulsive action. Third, it provides a ready to execute research design that separates monitoring from information acquisition and allows the proposed causal chain to be tested rather than merely asserted.

detail.abstract: Boreal forest fires are a large and underpriced source of carbon emissions. Yet the vast, remote zones where these fires burn are largely left unmanaged: values at risk are low, dispatch is costly, and detection usually arrives too late for initial attack to succeed. We quantify the climate value of closing this detection gap, using the FireSat satellite constellation as a concrete case. Combining nineteen years of spatially explicit fire and carbon data from the NASA ABoVE Fire Emission Database with the value-of-information and cost-plus-net-value-change economic frameworks, we estimate the carbon emissions avoided when early detection allows remote fires to be attacked before they escape, and value these avoided emissions at the social cost of carbon. Focusing on the permafrost-rich ecoregions of Alaska and the Yukon, where fires have, on average, a net climate-warming effect over policy-relevant horizons, we estimate that early attack can be a cost-effective climate intervention. Because remote early attack has little precedent, not all costs and benefits can be quantified. Our initial estimates count the constellation’s capital cost, the incremental suppression expenditure that earlier attack requires, and the direct combustion emissions avoided. They omit, on the cost side, the fixed investment in aircraft and crews that remote attack may require, the forgone ecological benefits of fire, and the albedo and aerosol cooling that avoided fires surrender; on the benefit side, fire-induced permafrost-thaw emissions, non-CO2 species, and air-quality, health, and property co-benefits; and, lowering the benefit, post-fire regrowth and the risk that suppressed area burns later. The net direction of these omissions is ambiguous. Within that scope, early attack avoids emissions at roughly $2.80–9.08 per tonne of CO2, implying a benefit-to-cost ratio of 20–66 to one, depending on how much of the management gap early attack closes. At our central assumptions, the ratio remains above one at every social cost of carbon we consider. At $185 per tonne, and if the agency faces a population of candidate ignitions close to the one our data resolve, it remains above one even if the agency cannot distinguish which ignitions will escape. Our results suggest that early wildfire detection in carbon-rich boreal landscapes merits serious consideration as a climate mitigation lever.

detail.abstract: Does prohibiting payday lending help or harm consumers? Using a county-year panel merging Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint data with state payday lending laws, we exploit within-county variation to show that prohibiting payday lending is associated with reduction in consumer financial complaints by 90 percent. Critically, fewer than 1 percent of the reduction involves complaints against payday lenders directly. Instead, credit reporting complaints account for 89 percent of the total effect, with significant reductions in debt collection, credit card, mortgage, and large-bank complaints-a pattern consistent with a financial distress cascade that extends beyond the payday market. Text analysis of complaint narratives is consistent with the cascade at the micro level: Downstream complaints in states permitting payday lending disproportionately mention payday-related terms, providing additional support for the proposed cascade mechanism. Prohibition is also associated with a 7.4 percentage point lower probability of explanation-only closure for complaints against payday lenders. Effects concentrate in highpoverty, high-inequality, and concentrated-banking counties. Household-level evidence from the Federal Reserve's SHED survey corroborates these patterns: Residents of payday-prohibiting states report significantly greater ability to cover emergency expenses, and payday loan use decreases among lowincome, low-education, and minority households.

detail.abstract: We study how childhood neighbors influence occupational choices and later-life earnings. Using linked census records for over 10 million children and historic census sheet microgeography, we find that growing up next door to someone in a given occupation increases the probability of being in that occupation as an adult by 10 percent relative to other children on the same street. The transmission effect is higher with more intense exposure, more connected neighborhoods, and between more similar families. Exposure to high-income or highly educated neighbors has lasting economic effects, leading to significant gains in adult income and education.

detail.abstract: Nursing homes face persistent staffing shortages and rely heavily on immigrant workers, particularly in direct-care occupations. This paper examines the effect of the 2025 expansion of Section 287(g), which delegates immigration enforcement authority to local law enforcement agencies, on nursing home labor supply. Exploiting the staggered county-level rollout of 287(g) agreements and using the Borusyak et al. (2024) imputation estimator, I find that 287(g) adoption reduces contract nursing hours by 37.2 hours per facility per month, while employed staffing is unaffected. Among contract nurses, certified nursing assistants (CNAs) are the most affected. The contract staffing reduction is concentrated among low-quality and large facilities, driven primarily by the task force model that authorizes street-level enforcement during routine police encounters, and is larger in counties with high foreign-born and Hispanic population shares and among not-for-profit facilities. These patterns are consistent with chilling effects rather than direct deportation: enforcement-induced fear propagates through immigrant social networks and suppresses the supply of temporary nursing staff where those networks are densest. These findings demonstrate that local immigration enforcement imposes unintended costs on the long-term care sector by disrupting the contract labor supply on which nursing homes, particularly those already providing lower-quality care, depend.

detail.abstract: We develop a model of electoral competition that captures the dynamic interaction between the incumbent's policy making and the informed opposition's response. An incumbent has an opportunity to introduce a reform. If the incumbent introduces the reform, the opposition can either acquiesce to it or promise to repeal it. Parties know whether the reform is partisan or common interest, but the voter does not. The voter observes the parties' decisions and decides which party to elect for the next period. We show that parties' platforms converge on the choice that is best for the voter only if common-interest reforms are sufficiently valuable, the incumbent is strongly office motivated, and the opposition is not. When these conditions fail, the opposition commits to policy repeal even when the incumbent's reform is common interest. Such inefficient repeals induce the incumbent to either forego common-interest reforms (gridlock) or double down on partisan reforms (policy divergence). In the latter case, some common-interest reforms are introduced, but then are subsequently repealed with positive probability, while some of the partisan reforms survive.

detail.abstract: In difference-indifferences with a continuous treatment, the regression of the change in the outcome on the dose mixes the average causal response with two biases, a differential trend across doses and selection on gains, which arises when units that receive larger doses would also respond differently to the same dose. Pre-period placebo slopes can benchmark the trend but say nothing about selection. We show that predetermined covariates measure the part of selection that runs through them, and we bound the rest by the sorting of the strongest observed group of covariates, while covariate-adjusted placebo slopes bound the trend. This gives an identified set for the average causal response, a confidence set that is valid at any trend and selection budget, and breakdown values for both. In the China shock, the covariates account for about half of the naive slope. The reduced form keeps its sign under moderate trends and selection, while the effect of U.S. import exposure is too imprecise to sign.

detail.abstract: Conservation practices that reduce nutrient runoff on agricultural lands, such as controlleddrainage, saturated buffers, and wetland restoration, are adopted at rates well below rates required to support federal water quality targets in the U.S. Midwest despite significant cost-share incentives. Using survey data from 530 farm operators across the Corn Belt, we ask:when farmers are offered a 50% government cost-share for conservation drainage practices,who would take it up and why? Probit models show that neighbor adoption reduces non-acceptance probability by 12.3 percentage points for controlled drainage, while higher liability-to-asset ratios consistently increase responsiveness to financial incentives across all practices. Latent class analysis identifies four distinct farmer segments, signifying heterogeneities that uniform programs fail to address. An additionality analysis for controlled drainage finds that targeting farmers who state a high likelihood of adopting under cost-share could raise adoption by as much as 73%, at an estimated government cost of approximately $2.1 billion across the study region, roughly half the cost of broader untargeted programs. These results indicate that significant adoption gains are achievable at moderate cost, but only through differentiated policy approaches that align intervention design with the heterogeneous barriers farmers face.

detail.abstract: How could inequality between social classes have ever persisted during the Malthusian epoch, as affluence led to greater reproductive success, diluting inherited wealth and narrowing disparities over time? This paper uncovers the Paradox of Inequality, establishes its robust theoretical foundations, and provides its resolution. The analysis suggests that elites’ lavish, nonproductive displays of status inadvertently diverted resources from reproduction, limiting the dilution of inherited wealth and sustaining inequality across generations. Ironically, extravagance preserved the wealth it seemed to squander.

detail.abstract: In 2013, the European Union Common Agricultural Policy introduced a set of compulsory greening measures in its subsidies scheme in order to achieve environmental goals. We analyse the impact of this reform on bird diversity in France. We match bird observations from the French Breeding Bird Survey (BBS) to parcel level information on agricultural land use and type of crops. We exploit the heterogeneous exposure of bird observation sites to the reform depending on their ex-ante extent of arable area in a continuous difference-in-differences approach. We find evidence of an increase in overall bird abundance after 2015 in sites with a higher ex-ante proportion of arable land, driven by a small number of generalist species, and no impact on species richness and phylogenetic diversity. A decomposition by diet type suggests that vertebrate eaters were positively impacted by the reform. By contrast, cropland species experienced the most dramatic decline after 2015 in sites with a higher share of arable area. Estimations of the dynamic effects of the reform suggest that the observed positive effects of the reform on bird abundance were limited to the first two years after its implementation. Based on observational data, our findings confirm previous concerns regarding the effectiveness of the 2013 reform in preserving biodiversity.

detail.abstract: Qualitative researchers frequently distinguish interpretivism from realism as if the reality of subjective experience required an ontology in which reality itself depends on subjective interpretation. This tutorial argues that the two claims should be separated. Human interpretations are subjectively experienced but ontologically real, embodied, historically formed, socially mediated, and potentially causally consequential. Drawing on critical realism, interpretive sociology, cognitive and affective psychology, situated cognition, identity theory, and game theory, the paper develops a non-reductionist, cross-level account connecting external events, bodily and neural processes, meaning-making, identity, strategic expectations, action, and institutional reproduction. Its claim is not that neuroscience proves critical realism or that social meanings can be reduced to physiology. Rather, embodied cognition supplies an explanatory interface through which interpretations can be investigated as processes within one differentiated reality. The paper contrasts ontological, epistemological, methodological, and semantic claims; distinguishes experience from the truth of its explanation; and shows why socially constituted objects can nevertheless be objectively consequential. It develops a transparent heuristic model, two worked organisational examples, and a stepwise qualitative research protocol. The tutorial explicitly complements Callaghan’s (2026) preceding paper, Narratives as Mechanisms: Bridging Social Constructionism and Critical Realism in Qualitative Analysis. Where that paper follows socially circulated narratives through cognitive uptake, institutionalisation, and consequence, the present paper clarifies the ontology of the experiencing and interpreting actor and extends the account toward identity dependent strategic interaction. The intended contribution is pedagogical and integrative rather than a claim to have originated realist interpretivism.

detail.abstract: We rebuild the displayed outright order book of NYMEX crude oil (CL) and Henry Hub natural gas (NG) futures order by order from CME market-by-order data. We compare 29 releases of the EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report and 31 releases of the Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report (March to October 2026) with four matched control days each, under pre-registered analysis plans. After the release, depth within five ticks of the mid stays depleted beyond normal days: over the first five minutes after the price reaction the book is missing the equivalent of 33.8 extra seconds of all of its normal near-mid depth in crude and 48.3 seconds in gas. Before the release, depth at the best price is withdrawn without extra cancellation. Before crude releases, cancellations make up a smaller share of the touch withdrawal than on matched days, and missing new orders take up the slack, becoming about as large a channel as cancels (0.38 vs 0.42). About 60% of the cancel-share contrast also appears at 10:30 before the gas report. Before gas releases, more resting orders execute. Release days are Wednesdays and Thursdays and control days are not, so these effects cannot be separated from a Wednesday and Thursday 10:30 effect. We then score the queue position estimators used by open-source backtesters against order-ID ground truth on 141 crude and 125 gas sessions. Their mean absolute fill-time errors range from 0.31 to 1.07 seconds in crude and 0.68 to 1.98 seconds in gas. Their shadow-order fill-rate and P&L biases are small, and their sign depends on how a true fill is read (post hoc). detail.abstract: Why do balanced portfolios lose protection when they need it? This article synthesizes theories of economic memory, endogenous laws, and feasible risk transfer to develop hedge survival: the conditional response of protective assets across economic states, loss severities, and investment horizons. The theory yields a portfolio protection account, a repair-horizon distinction, and a cost-aware allocation rule. A transparent, externally anchored laboratory separates public-market anchors from design assumptions and evaluates equities, Treasuries, gold, and cash under matched execution policies. With conservative return assumptions, conditional information adds about sixteen basis points of annual mean-variance value over stationary allocation and ten over a return-based covariance model. An equally informed statistical learner ties. State allocations, trading charges, tail losses, outcome dispersion, and failure scenarios explain the result. A separate joint-loss insurance experiment shows why valuable protection need not have positive expected profit. The contribution is an integrated financial measurement and implementation framework, illustrated by reproducible simulations; historical incremental forecasting value remains to be established. Key Takeaways • Inherited response, endogenous economic laws, and feasible trading capacity determine whether protection survives. A condition-and horizon-dependent hedge response translates those economic mechanisms into a portfolio protection account. • Matched simulations separate information from execution. Conservative return assumptions reveal smaller risk budgets, little demand for gold, meaningful conditional information value, and a tie with an equally informed statistical model. • Hedge-failure insurance can improve portfolio welfare while losing money on average. Positive expected trading profit requires a forecast advantage large enough to cover the quoted premium, financing, and implementation costs.

detail.abstract: This study compares two inspection mechanisms for promoting cooperation in a public goods game. The mechanisms differ in which players are selected for inspection. In a repeated two-stage game, players in each period first choose their network neighbors and then choose contributions to a local public good that benefits both themselves and their neighbors. The random inspection mechanism selects one player with equal probability, while the targeted inspection mechanism selects one of the players with the fewest neighbors. Theoretically, targeted inspection is more effective in promoting cooperation. Under both mechanisms, cooperation can be sustained in equilibrium when players sever links with less cooperative neighbors, leaving less cooperative players with fewer neighbors and therefore higher inspection probabilities under targeted inspection. However, experimental results show that targeted inspection leads to lower cooperation than random inspection. Participants under targeted inspection tend to maintain more links to reduce their likelihood of being inspected rather than severing links with less cooperative neighbors.

detail.abstract: Solar and wind power account for a growing share of electricity generation in China and now dominate new capacity additions. As the power system transitions toward renewable generation, greater flexibility will be required to maintain system stability. This paper uses a computable general equilibrium model to assess the macroeconomic implications of this transition. Model results indicate a modest increase in electricity prices in the near-term, followed by sustained declines as renewable shares rise, particularly when variability is managed through battery storage rather than coal-fired backup generation. While the transition requires substantial adjustments in electricity supply and investment, it raises GDP in the long run and strengthens energy security. Battery-based flexibility outperforms continued reliance on coal across multiple dimensions, even when accounting for rising electricity demand from emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. However, this transition pathway also increases the risk of stranded assets in the coal power sector.

detail.abstract: Background: Monitoring the safety of medical products is a core pharmacovigilance concern. To support drug safety assessment, Spontaneous Reporting Systems (SRS) collect reports of suspected adverse events of approved medical products, offering a critical resource for identifying potential safety concerns that may not emerge during clinical trials. Modern nonparametric empirical Bayes methods are flexible statistical approaches that can accurately identify and estimate the strength of the association between an adverse event and a drug from SRS data. However, there is currently no comprehensive and easily accessible implementation of these methods.Methods: We introduce an open-source R package pvEBayes, which implements a suite of nonparametric empirical Bayes methods (including general-gamma, K-gamma, Koenker-Mizera (KM) method, Efron's approach and Gamma-Poisson Shrinker (GPS)) for pharmacovigilance, along with post-processing tools and graphical summaries for streamlining the application of these methods. The package is openly available on the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN), and has passed rOpenSci peer review with a gold badge. A simulation study is provided to examine the performance of the general-gamma method with different hyperparameter selection. In addition, detailed examples are provided to demonstrate the application of the package through analyses of two real-world SRS datasets, statin2025_44 and gbca2025_69, curated from the publicly available U.S. Food & Drug Administration's Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database.Results: The simulation study confirms that the general-gamma method is robust to the choice of its hyperparameter α: Akaike information criterion- and Bayesian information criterion-based selection both perform well. The usage of the pvEBayes package is illustrated by analysis of statin2025_44 and gbca2025_69 datasets.

detail.abstract:
Regime changes concentrate most market losses and opportunities, yet they are usually recognised only in hindsight. This paper presents Epistemic Symmetry Theory (EST), a framework that reads regime structure in the narrative that precedes prices. News items are routed to domain "hyperspaces" and scored by language models against questions that encode expectations, in the spirit of the forward-looking macroeconomic framework recognised by the 2026 Nobel Prize to Hall and Woodford. Each item becomes a small cloud of points; from many items the framework estimates a manifold of current expectations, local viewpoints, and a connection given by the orthogonal Procrustes alignment of successive viewpoints. The structure is classified through the Coxeter form of the admissible angles between its dominant directions. We specify a two-stage detector that flags a candidate "trauma" when an item arrives, confirms or absorbs it on the following items, and classifies the change as a jump, a rotation of the connection, or a full trauma. On synthetic data, 60 runs per type, the detector confirms 115-117 of 120 traumas within a median of 6-7 items, classifies jumps and full traumas almost without error and rotations in 87% of cases, and absorbs isolated shocks in 90% of runs. The simulation also documents a weakness: after a rotation, the manifold widens and false confirmations rise from 0.05 to 0.36 per hyperspace per run. The framework does not forecast prices. The full narrative pipeline has not yet been tested on real news; we state the tests that would falsify it.
AI disclosure: Generative AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were used to assist with drafting and editing the text and with writing the simulation code. The author designed the framework, reviewed all content and code, and takes full responsibility for the paper.

detail.abstract: We show that the equivalence between competitive equilibrium and constrained efficiency asserted in Proposition 4 of Finster, Goldberg, and Lock (2025) fails in both directions under their stated assumption of monotone increasing and concave valuations. detail.abstract: Inflation is rarely a uniform process; it propagates through complex, non-linear interactions between heterogeneous economic sectors. This paper proposes a novel methodological framework for analyzing the internal dynamics of inflation in Spain by modeling the Consumer Price Index as a complex directed network. Utilizing the COICOP (Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose) disaggregation, we apply Bivariate Transfer Entropy to quantify the directed flow of information between price indices. Our approach captures non-linear dependencies and the inherent asymmetry in price setting without assuming Gaussian distributions. By applying the Louvain community detection algorithm to undirected networks, we identify functional "price clusters" that transcend administrative classifications. Our empirical results reveal a structure in which energy and transport sectors serve as primary information drivers (sources), while service sectors largely act as information basins. The empirical results have direct implications for the design and communication of monetary policy; likewise, the study suggests that certain easily implemented policies targeting sectors that act as "nodes" generate stabilizing effects within the aggregate network.

detail.abstract: Changes in uncertainty can arise from movements in its upside and downside tails. Real-option and growth-option models predict that these tail movements influence firms' investment decisions through distinct channels. We test these predictions by examining how tail-specific tariff uncertainty shocks affect firms' plans. We conducted a survey experiment with large Chinese exporters using hypothetical future-tariff scenarios. Consistent with the real-option model, downside-tail uncertainty significantly affects planned employment and multiple investment margins, although the responses are asymmetric between increases and decreases in downside uncertainty. Upside-tail uncertainty has weaker effects on average, but their direction is consistent with the growth-option model. Finally, greater irreversibility amplifies the real-option response while dampening the growth-option response, as predicted by the option models, respectively. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of distinguishing upside from downside uncertainty and accounting for the reversibility of firms' decisions.

detail.abstract: Anomaly returns concentrate around information releases, suggesting mispricing that is corrected as news arrives. We replicate 94 accounting-based anomalies with accounting data lagged by up to five years. Alpha decays slowly: median monthly CAPM alphas are 36 basis points at the four-month lag and 28 with year-old data, robust out of sample and positive internationally. An equal-weighted book of year-old factors earns 19 basis points monthly (𝑡 = 4.9); the four-month-minus-twelve-month spread earns 8 (𝑡 = 6.0) and is shrinking. title: Noise-Corrected Tests for High-Dimensional Forecasting Models

detail.abstract:
A forecasting model that estimates many parameters adds estimation noise to its forecasts.
Classical theory treats this noise as of order $P/T$, so a longer window removes it. When the
number of parameters grows with the window, it does not. For ridge forecasts the noise
converges to $\sigma^2\Psi(c,z)$, a closed-form function of the ratio $c=P/T$ and the ridge
penalty $z$. Two questions then come apart. Does the enlarged model forecast better at this
window, and does its systematic part beat the benchmark once estimation noise is set aside?
The Diebold--Mariano test answers the first. I propose a test of the second. Where the
Clark--West statistic adds back the realised squared forecast differential, the
noise-corrected statistic adds back only what estimation noise is expected to contribute to
it. It is computable inside any ridge forecasting loop and asymptotically normal, with a
long-run variance that allows for overlapping estimation windows. The closed form also
predicts the window at which a detected signal starts to pay. On a panel of realized-variance
series where the enlarged model almost always forecasts worse,
Clark--West rejects in its favour on $75$ to $87$ percent of the series that pass a check on
the correction, and the noise-corrected statistic on at most $7$ percent.

detail.abstract: We study the effects of low-intensity tax enforcement on VAT compliance among newly registered firms in Norway using a large-scale randomized field experiment. Around 20,000 firms were randomly assigned to desk-based audits, informational letters, phone-based guidance, or a control group. Desk-based audits uncover non-compliance in over nine percent of cases, corresponding to an estimated VAT gap of about 5.6 percent. However, results show no evidence of behavioral responses to any of the three interventions. The estimates are sufficiently precise to rule out even small compliance effects, suggesting that low-intensity VAT enforcement, in isolation, is insufficient to generate persistent change in the firms' average VAT reports.

detail.abstract: Understanding the linkages between real and financial markets is important for a range of economic agents, including policymakers, investors (in both market types) and those engaged in modelling behaviour. This paper argues that financial market correlations (both across international stocks and between stocks and bonds) carries information about subsequent economic conditions. Higher perceived risk results in investor selling all stocks (higher stock correlation) and buying bonds (lower stock and bond correlation), such that a movement in correlations acts as an indicator of future performance. Where investors expect more benign economic conditions, they are more likely to build a balanced stock and bond portfolio (lower stock and higher stock and bond correlations). Using a monthly G7 data set, correlations (constructed from daily data) reveal a negative relation from international stock correlations and a positive relation from stock and bonds correlations for subsequent economic growth and stock returns. The predictive results are robust to the inclusion of alternative risk measures, suggesting that the correlations contain unique information, and to alternative (confounding) views (and modelling) on the relation between risk and the correlations. Further robustness checks involve different approaches for construction of the correlation series and sample periods. While movements in these correlations provide signals to a range of agents, we examine the likely drivers of the predictive relation as an important extension. This reveals that the correlations appear to impact demand-side factors (consumption and inflation) rather than supply-side (investment and productivity). Overall, this paper provides information both in the form of signals for policymakers and investors to act, as well as to enhance our understanding of the linkages between real and financial markets.

detail.abstract: Extreme year-to-year changes in governance indicators occur far more often than Gaussian models predict. Using the 2026 update of the Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI) for 216 economies, 1996-2025, this study characterises the distribution of changes in a six-indicator composite, handling biennial reporting before 2003 and incomplete composites explicitly and conditioning on the published standard errors by country and by observation. Among the 75% of countries with the most precise estimates, changes beyond four standard deviations occur 89 times as often as under a Gaussian, excess kurtosis is 4.7, the quantile tail ratio is 4.09 against 2.91, and a t distribution with 3.5 degrees of freedom fits far better than a normal. The pattern appears in all six dimensions, under alternative composites, after removing year effects and after standardising by each country's own volatility, and a Gaussian measurement-noise model scaled to the published standard errors reproduces little of it (excess kurtosis about 0.2). Consecutive changes are positively correlated (0.11, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.16), whereas transitory noise implies a correlation near-0.5. The composite shows no robust directional asymmetry: skewness stays between 0.07 and 0.12 and is statistically indistinguishable from zero in every sample built from complete composites, while the full panel gives values from-1.69 to +1.94 depending on data handling. The results support heavy-tailed error specifications when modelling WGI changes and call for caution with claims of directional asymmetry.

detail.abstract: Why does the stock market remain resilient, attract capital, and recover quickly from crises, even when aggregate returns are low and conventional metrics signal overvaluation? This paper uncovers a hidden, self-sustaining mechanism: the corporate self-financing cycle. When monetary policy raises the cost of capital, firms, most of which have below-unity betas, respond with share buybacks, compressing the equity denominator and mechanically restoring the aggregate return on equity (AROE). This is not financial engineering; it is an accounting-based defense mechanism rooted in the balance-sheet identity. Using an ARDL model with Newey-West HAC estimation on U.S. nonfinancial corporate data (1985-2025), I provide empirical evidence for each phase of the cycle. Past merger volumes trigger buybacks; buybacks stabilize ROE; and, with a lag of four to five years, the capital returned to shareholders is redeployed into productive investments, generating growth in Gross Value Added. The cycle is synchronized by common exposure to the oscillation of the 3-month Treasury bill rate. The findings challenge the narrative that buybacks are a form of "predatory value extraction." They suggest instead that the market is not a fragile mechanism but an adaptive, self-correcting system-one in which corporate managers act as silent stabilizers, and capital is continuously recycled to its most productive uses.

detail.abstract: Comparative research on the far right in Europe concentrates mostly on Western Europe, neglecting the distinct dynamics and continuities in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE). However, when CEE is analysed, Hungary and Poland are often wrongly treated as representative of the region. This chapter offers a comparative overview of the far right in CEE, examining parties, voter behaviour and the broader dynamics of mainstreaming and radicalisation. It highlights that far-right parties in CEE are a phenomenon “sui generis”: while they share core ideological markers of nativism and authoritarianism with their Western counterparts, they emerged from the post-communist transformation and targeted ethnic and sexual minorities as key enemies of the state. Accordingly, anti-immigrant attitudes used to be a weaker predictor of far-right support in CEE. However, the 2015 “refugee crisis” in part “westernised” the far right’s agenda in CEE, shifting the emphasis towards immigration. Meanwhile, as cordon sanitaires against the far right have largely been absent, the radicalisation of the mainstream rather than the mainstreaming of the far right has been a defining dynamic in CEE. The chapter concludes that far-right parties in the East and West are converging and calls for more research on intra-regional variation and understudied cases such as the Baltic states.

detail.abstract:
A 2026 OECD study argues that China’s rising industrial subsidies explain much of its global market share gains, but the study's flawed methodology, particularly in measuring interest rate subsidies, may overstate the scale of government support.  In contrast, a 2025 IMF study finds that China’s industrial subsidies have remained broadly stable as a share of GDP, challenging the OECD’s conclusion that subsidies are increasing.  Because of their flaws, these studies do not provide useful guidance for policymakers trying to judge the magnitude of Chinese industrial subsidies. Future studies on subsidies should improve their methodology, including by fully disclosing the data on which they base their estimates and by explaining why their estimates differ from prior studies.

The differing findings of the OECD and IMF studies highlight the challenges of accurately measuring Chinese industrial subsidies, making the estimates unreliable for shaping trade policy. Policymakers should avoid using disputed figures to justify protectionism. Greater data transparency and clearer explanations for discrepancies between estimates are essential to help policymakers formulate effective trade policies.

detail.abstract: Whether climate stress displaces people or traps them in place is unresolved. The common intuition is displacement: crops fail, heat becomes unliveable and people leave. Other work predicts the opposite for poor countries, where migration abroad is expensive and the shock that sharpens the wish to leave can destroy the means to go. Estimates disagree, partly because realized temperature mixes warming that households anticipated with warming they did not. I isolate the unanticipated part with temperature forecast errors, the warmth or cold a forecast missed, and estimate their effect on monthly international migration from countries holding most of the world’s population. Here I show that unexpected warmth does not detectably move migration on average, but that in low-income countries an unexpectedly hot month lowers departures over the following year. No richer income group shows a detectable response. The migration suppression is strongest where incomes depend on agriculture, also appears outside the growing season and leaves in-migration flat, consistent with heat removing the means to move. For the poorest countries, unexpected heat may hold people back rather than push them abroad. Projections and policies built around displacement may overstate departures from these countries and overlook those who cannot afford to leave.

detail.abstract: Who receives returning family experience can determine whether fertility recovery survives temporary support. An overlapping-generations model combines marriage, fertility, child investment and mobility. Recipient allocation, source visibility and low-parent upward mobility share the same first-entry response when the low-parent source is absent. Allocation isolates an information channel at fixed resources and mobility, preserving initial mean beliefs under neutral visibility. On nonempty open parameter regions, one allocation sustains parenthood after sufficiently long finite support while another returns to exclusion after every finite hold. Near exclusion, first-update differences are bounded by the raresource share. Local derivatives distinguish allocation from mobility and locate changes in stationary recovery windows. Numerical experiments separately verify actual withdrawal paths and report comparable expenditure, population and adjustment measures. The analysis connects information-source reproduction to persistent low fertility and states the measurements needed to distinguish this mechanism empirically.

detail.abstract: We study how background risk affects optimal liability rules in a unilateral accident model with risk-averse parties. Under negligence, background risk borne by a prudent victim raises the optimal due-care standard relative to the benchmark case without background risk. detail.abstract: Households search harder when they borrow than when they invest. Using the Survey of Consumer Finances from 1995 to 2025, we compare each household's search for the best terms in the two domains. Among households holding both debt and financial assets, borrowing search exceeds investing search by 0.69 points on a zero-to-ten scale when the stakes are equal-a gap we call the Defensive Search Premium. Relative stakes explain little of it, and it is largest where interest is actually being paid. We model households that code payments as losses and divide a limited search budget across domains. As the model predicts, search pays only in its own domain: borrowing search lowers mortgage and auto-loan rates while investing search does not, and tilting search toward borrowing reduces holdings of higher-yielding certificates of deposit. Households fight hardest where they pay, and they pay for it where they earn.

detail.abstract: Do households that plan far ahead buy a few stocks and hold them, or trade less? We model an investor who chooses how many stocks to hold and how often to trade them, with the planning horizon raising the value of diversification and a limited attention budget governing trading. Using the Survey of Consumer Finances from 1989 to 2025, we find that long-horizon investors hold broader portfolios-more stocks, fewer single-stock positions, and more funds-but do not trade any position more intensively. The planning horizon affects trading only through portfolio breadth. Total trades rise with the number of stocks with an elasticity of 0.38, rejecting the view that investors treat each stock as a separate account. The model's cross-equation restrictions hold: the horizon effect on trading equals the breadth effect scaled by this elasticity. Long horizons make portfolios broader, not busier.

title: Rebuilding Operation Safe Corridor into a Legitimate and Evidence Based Disengagement, Deradicalisation, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (DDRR) System in Nigeria
affiliations: National Defence College, Nigeria

detail.title: Rebuilding Operation Safe Corridor into a Legitimate and Evidence Based Disengagement, Deradicalisation, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (DDRR) System in Nigeria

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: Operation Safe Corridor (OSC) is Nigeria's principal non-kinetic pathway for people associated with Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) who are assessed as suitable for disengagement, rehabilitation and reintegration. Yet its public legitimacy has not kept pace with its strategic importance. This paper reexamines the programme as a Disengagement, Deradicalisation, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (DDRR) system operating during an active conflict rather than as a conventional postwar DDR programme. It uses qualitative document analysis of Nigerian policy instruments, official statements, programme reporting, court information, United Nations material and peer-reviewed and policy literature published between 2015 and October 2026. A trend and pattern analysis distinguishes the reported surrender population from the much smaller, screened OPSC client population. It finds that the available figures cannot support a genuine acceptance or success rate because they combine combatants, spouses, children and other associates, while excluding the unknown numbers screened out, detained, prosecuted, transferred or released through other channels. The programme's main weakness is therefore not the existence of rehabilitation; it is an incomplete accountability architecture around it. Opaque risk categorisation, camp-centred and time-bound programming, uncertain legal referral pathways, thin community consent, weak victim parity and unpublished outcome data make the system vulnerable to both security failure and political rejection. Drawing on Nigeria's community reconciliation practice and Colombia's institutionalised reintegration system, the article proposes a Nigerian DDRR Compact: a statutory, civilian-led and security-supported system that separates criminal liability from reintegration eligibility, applies individual case plans, funds host communities and victims, and publishes independently audited outcomes. The argument is that surrender is a necessary opening, but not evidence of reintegration. Sustainable exit from violent extremism depends on lawful sorting, credible community repair and measurable post-release support.

detail.abstract: Factor-augmented VARs (FAVARs) combine latent factors extracted from large panels with factors that are assumed to be perfectly observed. We relax this assumption by treating individual variables as noisy factor proxies. Our proposed estimation approach iterates between principal component extraction and reduced-rank regression and allows multiple proxies to inform factor estimation. The estimated factors are shown to be consistent in the presence of weak factors. A group-lasso extension enables sparse proxy selection, and a cross-validation scheme jointly selects model dimensions and tuning parameters. Monte Carlo evidence shows that the method substantially improves factor estimation and forecasting with weak factors, and reduces bias in structural impulse response estimation when observable factor proxies are measured with error. We document the usefulness of our approach in a recursive pseudo-out-of-sample bond return forecasting analysis.

title: Reliability and Workflow Assurance in Generative AI for Legal Practice
affiliations: Durham College

detail.title: Reliability and Workflow Assurance in Generative AI for Legal Practice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Background. Generative artificial intelligence can assist legal research, document analysis and drafting. Its professional value also depends on grounding, issue completeness, applicable legal authority, verification work and continuity of decisions. Objective. To map practice-relevant empirical evidence on reliability and workflow assurance, distinguish measured benefits from limitations, and identify testable implications for a proposed Legal Decision Memory product. Methods. An AI-assisted rapid review used bounded OpenAlex and arXiv searches on 5 October 2026, capped at 200 records per index, supplemented by targeted searches. Deduplication reduced 400 indexed records to 368 candidate clusters; 182 advanced or remained unclear after AI screening and reassessment. Accessible primary reports underwent extraction and qualitative appraisal; professional guidance was considered separately. Review processes were AI-only and remain provisional, without independent human verification. No prospective registration or meta-analysis was completed; this was not a full systematic review. Results. The register contained 123 reports, including 8 conditional adjuncts, in 122 known linked report families. Student experiments, small drafting comparisons and descriptive deployments supported task specific benefits. Citation existence, proposition support, issue omissions, legal-version selection and reviewed work time remained distinct outcomes. Some retrieval, prompting and escalation configurations improved targeted outcomes without establishing general legal correctness. Temporal and multi-turn benchmarks provided direct evidence. Synthetic cross-session results and descriptive correction records offered limited continuity evidence but did not validate transfer or reuse of approved decisions after changed facts, permissions or handover. Conclusions. The evidence supports conditional assistance with explicit inspection and review. It does not establish industry-wide failure prevalence, current vendor rankings or an error-free product. Legal Decision Memory implications remain unvalidated; future evaluations should measure approved work and continuity across context changes.

detail.abstract: How does the design of the tax system affect firms' formalisation decisions? To answer this question, this paper develops a quantitative model in which heterogeneous firms choose whether to operate formally or informally. Formal firms face three types of taxes: a turnover tax, a payroll tax, and a progressive profit tax, each with separate rates and thresholds. We calibrate the model to the observed firm size distributions of both formal and informal manufacturing establishments in India. Counterfactuals show that while an increase in all three tax rates leads to higher tax revenue, the effect on formalisation is non-uniform: a higher turnover tax rate increases formalisation, a higher payroll tax rate reduces formalisation, and a higher profit tax rate has negligible effects on formalisation. When tax instruments are chosen jointly to maximise welfare subject to an informality target and a revenue-preserving constraint, the optimal reforms shift taxation away from payroll taxes and toward turnover and profit taxation. Targeting an informal-firm share of 75 per cent increases welfare by 1.7 per cent while preserving tax revenue, showing that substantial formalisation can be achieved without sacrificing fiscal capacity or aggregate welfare.
