detail.abstract: We examine a household's optimal consumption and portfolio choice problem over a finite working life subject to unspanned labor income risk. To circumvent the twin mathematical intractabilities of time-dependence and market incompleteness, we introduce a dual-track framework. First, we develop a novel analytical approximation by replacing the deterministic lifecycle with an exponentially distributed random horizon, deriving a rigorous, timehomogeneous benchmark system of coupled integral equations. Second, we engineer a modelbased reinforcement learning (RL) approach. Under state-sensitivity conditions, we prove that for fixed smooth perturbations of a verified interior optimum, one exact Bellman correction yields second-order accuracy in the relative consumption error and portfolio-weight error. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that optimal consumption rates and risky asset allocations decline deterministically as retirement approaches, driven by heightened precautionary motives under compounding income volatility and risk aversion. These structural insights deliver immediate operational value for designing scalable, equitable automated wealth-advising engines.

detail.abstract: This study explored the potential adoption of fermented organic fertilizers (FOFs) made from fruit and crop waste using brown sugar as a fermenting agent, as a sustainable solution to soil degradation and climate stress in Bugesera District, Rwanda. The purpose was to assess the feasibility of integrating FOFs into smallholder farming practices to improve soil health and support climate-resilient agriculture. A mixed-methods approach was used, combining a descriptive quantitative design with a qualitative case study strategy. The study involved 100 survey respondents and 25 interview participants, including farmers, extension officers, and a cooperative leader. Quantitative results showed that 66.3% of farmers regularly used organic fertilizers, while 45.5% relied on a combination of organic and chemical inputs. Although 71.3% had heard of organic fertilizers, most were unaware of the specific FOF process. However, 79.2% expressed willingness to adopt FOFs if training and materials were provided. Qualitative findings confirmed strong interest but identified barriers such as limited knowledge, cost of sugar, and lack of follow-up support. The study concluded that FOFs are a promising but underutilized innovation. Future research should test long-term impacts on soil productivity and develop scalable training models to support widespread adoption.

detail.abstract: In the twenty-first century, many major economies have entered a high-debt development model, and China is no exception. Theoretically, a national macroeconomic balance sheet should first be established, and monetary quantity should then be studied in conjunction with it. The analysis must rest on the identity that asset-side and debt-side money supply represent the same quantity of money circulating at different velocities. An assetsmoney-debt simultaneous-equation model explains why China experienced relatively high CPI inflation during the earlier reform period but persistently weak price changes later. Starting from the causal mechanism of macro-balance-sheet repair, the model also demonstrates how repair of micro balance sheets can lead to inadequate macroeconomic liquidity and slower growth. China now faces this problem, and the model can characterize both its structural condition and the degree of distortion. The paper therefore proposes coordinating assets and debt and promoting market-oriented restructuring as practical approaches to governing deflation.

detail.abstract: Whether a factor works is a property not of the factor alone but of the factor and the market segment together. A significance hurdle read in one segment discards factors alive in another. Of 179 anomalies, the 94 a |t| < 1.96 screen rejects in large-cap stocks earn an out-of-sample Sharpe of 0.85, but 1.30 reallocated as a group to the small-cap segment they fit: a 3.8% six-factor alpha (t = 8.3), orthogonal to size and low volatility, reproduced out of sample in China. The correction has a ceiling: routing factors one at a time cannot beat the group move, because only their shared tilt survives estimation.

detail.abstract: We examine whether the physical co-location of corporate executive aircraft at regional reliever airports predicts pre-announcement stock price leakage and acquirer overpayment penalties in public corporate mergers and acquisitions. Using unencrypted Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) radio transponder logs mapped deterministically to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) registry records via the 24-bit ICAO24 hardware block, we apply Haversine spatial geofencing in DuckDB across a balanced panel of N = 250 corporate transactions between 2018 and 2026. Controlling for free cash flow agency costs, firm valuation (Tobin's Q), transaction scale, and cash financing, we document a statistically significant 214 basis point pre-announcement discount (p < 0.0001) in acquiring firm equity over the 15-day pre-deal event window (CAR[-15,-1]), net of short-borrow market frictions (300 bps Hard-to-Borrow fee and 10 bps slippage). We resolve ex-ante trade directionality using a deterministic capital asymmetry heuristic (Enterprise Value ratio ≥ 2.50) paired with options implied volatility skews. To establish causal identification, a 1,000-iteration Monte Carlo permutation placebo test scrambles meeting timestamps, yielding a mean placebo beta statistically indistinguishable from zero (p = 0.742). Furthermore, a pre-trend evaluation of CAR[-30,-16] yields a flat baseline (p = 0.5616), confirming that the physical flight summit represents the isolated structural trigger rather than pre-existing media rumors. Finally, an out-of-sample logistic classification engine achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.7632 and a Brier Score of 0.1648, demonstrating geospatial telematics as a viable, uncorrelated alternative data vector for institutional risk-arbitrage capital allocation.

detail.abstract: This work provides a systematic empirical investigation of the operational trade-off between automated feature complexity and regulatory parsimony in credit-scoring predictive modeling. While advanced machine learning algorithms are often proposed to capture non-linear relationships, traditional generalized linear models remain the industry standard because of their transparency. We investigate the boundary conditions of the so-called flat maximum effect by implementing a brute-force feature expansion engine, generating high-order polynomial interactions and pairwise ratios across eight benchmark datasets. To mirror operational constraints, we deploy a double-tournament model selection protocol coupled with a Post-LASSO feature filter, restricting the expanded functional spaces to K=15 non-zero regressors. Our out-of-sample predictions, validated via the non-parametric DeLong test for correlated ROC curves, indicate a heterogeneous landscape. The empirical evidence suggests that the marginal predictive utility of non-linear structural complexity depends heavily on the baseline informational maturity of each dataset analyzed. While combinatorial expansion yields measurable gains in raw retail portfolios lacking engineered features, it can degrade performance in accounting-based corporate repositories. Furthermore, when regulatory parsimony (the 15-variable constraint) is enforced, the performance of the restricted non-linear spaces generally converges to that of simple linear main effects. The methods proposed and applied in this work provide a framework for assessing when automated feature engineering yields statistically significant improvements over parsimonious linear baselines.

detail.abstract: Trust is critical for socioeconomic participation yet systematically lower among disadvantaged groups. Prior work assumes community norms shape trust by signaling behavioral prevalence and approval. We show that prevalence and approval do not suffice: the key factor is social expectation conditionality, the degree to which people attribute expectation-driven behavior to community members. Using vignette experiments with a nationally representative U.S. sample, we show normative cues generate trust inferences only when respondents attribute conditionality. This attribution is attenuated among economically and racially marginalized respondents, identifying a cognitive mechanism through which disadvantage sustains low trust. Where conditionality is attributed, communicating prosocial expectations can shift trust before behavioral change; where it is not, restoring the expectations-behavior link is the prior task. because repeated exposure to disorder attenuates the inferential link between normative cues and trustworthiness judgments. This account has direct implications for intervention: communicating credible prosocial expectations can shift trust judgments even before behavioral change occurs, but only where normative information is perceived as diagnostically meaningful.

detail.abstract: Why does manufacturing employment in emerging markets peak at half the levels advanced economies reached? We investigate this question through a quantitative trade model with structural change and rural-to-urban migration. Emerging markets have a comparative advantage in manufacturing, so trade alone should make them industrialize more, not less. Instead, we show that what holds them back are large rural-urban labor market wedges, which may reflect migration frictions or skill barriers. We estimate the wedges from wage gaps and migration flows. Without them, the median emerging economy does not prematurely deindustrialize, and instead reaches a peak manufacturing employment share roughly 10 percentage points higher than the data. By contrast, the rise of China contributes little to premature deindustrialization. Consistent with the model, we provide quasi-experimental evidence that a labor-saving agricultural technology increased industrialization in Brazil only in municipalities with young, mobile populations.

detail.abstract: Most studies on statistical arbitrage look at US markets, where borrow rates are predictable and commissions are near zero. India presents a very different reality: single-stock shorting in the cash market is essentially nonexistent due to an illiquid borrow market, forcing traders into futures where taxes and exchange fees eat directly into returns. In this paper, I test whether daily statistical arbitrage works on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) from 2010 to 2025. I track three common frameworks: classic distance pairs (Gatev et al. 2006), PCA-factor residual mean-reversion (Avellaneda & Lee 2010), and rolling machine learning models (Guijarro-Ordonez et al. 2021). On paper, without friction, the signals look remarkably strong: gross Sharpe ratios hit +0.95 to +1.74, with Newey-West t-statistics between +4.05 and +7.49. But as soon as you plug in real-world friction-the Securities Transaction Tax (especially after the October 2024 hike), stamp duties, GST, and turnover charges, alongside modest execution slippage-the entire strategy falls apart. Net Sharpe ratios plunge into deep negative territory (-1.63 to-2.96), burning capital at-16.7% to-25.9% each year. Break-even requires cutting costs down to 0.38x of actual institutional levels, which is legally impossible because statutory levies set a hard floor. Adding machine learning actually hurts net performance: while it catches short-term mispricings better on paper, it drives turnover up by 34%, handing even more capital over to taxes. Out of 12 pre-registered robustness tests, none pass multiple-testing corrections or the Deflated Sharpe Ratio. Overall, standalone daily statistical arbitrage simply cannot survive statutory friction in India, though the underlying displacement signals still hold practical promise for institutional execution timing.

detail.abstract: The life-cycle model assumes households plan over their remaining lifetime, yet in the Survey of Consumer Finances (1989-2025) more than a third of households plan their saving and spending no more than one year ahead. We develop a model in which the planning horizon is chosen and show that fundamentals-age, survival, retirement distance, and income uncertainty-cannot generate the short horizons observed. Liquidity frictions can. Credit-constrained and hand-to-mouth households, those in poor health, and recent bankruptcy filers plan horizons 18-31 percent shorter, holding income and wealth fixed. In the 2007-09 panel, the same household shortens its horizon by about 20 percent when it becomes hand-to-mouth or loses a job and lengthens it by a third when liquidity returns. Survival expectations explain the old-age decline in horizons but little else. Short horizons are an equilibrium response to liquidity, not a fixed preference.

detail.abstract: Climate change is reshaping wild fisheries by changing productivity, species distributions, and increasing environmental variability, with serious economic implications for fishing communities and global seafood markets. Concurrently, government policies ranging from quota systems and marine protected areas to subsidy reforms and enforcement strategies, play a critical role in mediating, and sometimes, aggravating these impacts. This selected review synthesizes literature published between 2000 and 2026 to examine how climate stressors and policy interventions jointly influence fisheries outcomes and their economic consequences. We analyze empirical, modeling, and policy-evaluation studies focusing exclusively on wild marine fisheries. The evidence suggests that well-designed governance can reduce climate-related economic risks by improving resilience, stabilizing revenues, and supporting adaptive capacity, whereas poorly aligned incentives often amplify vulnerability. Key research gaps include limited evaluation of distributional impacts, small-scale fisheries economics, and policy effectiveness under rapid climate extremes. The findings inform pathways toward climate-resilient and economically sustainable fisheries governance.

detail.abstract: Autonomous systems can increasingly prepare hazardous environments before people enter them: surveying sites, producing propellant, water and power, building shelter and testing habitats. When a destination can be prepared first, the decision to commit people to it no longer has to rest on a date; it can rest on evidence. This article develops the policy principles for that decision, taking crewed missions beyond Earth orbit as the main application. It argues that committing crews to a destination from which rescue is slow or impossible should depend on readiness demonstrated in place and verified independently. Treating the readiness decision as a test that can err in either direction, it shows why an operator deciding alone under schedule pressure will tend to accept too much risk of sending people to an unready destination. It then proposes a Verified Readiness Gate: ten readiness domains and their evidence; a comparison of four verification models; a dual-key rule under which departure requires both the operator's decision and an independent certification, within an authorisation by the authorising State; and a rollover rule that makes a launch date an eligible opportunity rather than a commitment. It also sets out wider principles for autonomous-first exploration, including transparent reporting of the costs of human presence, periodic reallocation of work between people and machines, and continued human-survival research where failure is recoverable. Existing instruments do not provide a specific destination-readiness certification framework for these decisions. The article shows how agencies, operators, authorising States and international partners could close the gap.

detail.abstract: This interdisciplinary paper explores how Albanian immigrants worldwide have tried to maintain their religious and national identity. The paper opens with a sociological and historical context of religious plurality in Albania. Next, the paper addresses how communist rule sought to suppress religion in Albania. Under this regime, leaving the country without permission was a crime, yet some Albanians managed to flee into exile. The paper then explores how their faith was preserved while they were in exile and the ways in which religious tolerance returned to Albania after communist rule. This paper also stresses the importance of well-being among Albanian immigrants, especially when they faced socioeconomic obstacles. Some of these barriers have included qualification mismatch and low wages. The paper then concludes by highlighting the concept of durim, meaning endurance or patience, which can empower Albanian immigrants when used in positive ways that promote self-advocacy. Going forward, this concept and the Albanian immigration experience in general would benefit from additional scholarship. This paper ultimately recommends that more researchers explore Albanian immigration from its history to its present sociological context, with an emphasis on how to best serve this population.

detail.abstract: Why do managerial styles persist even when managers turn over? detail.abstract: We study how the visibility of traders' positions relates to their influence on other market participants and their incentives to communicate in prediction markets. We exploit an April 2024 rule change on Polymarket that made each commenter's current position visible alongside the comment. After disclosure, comments backed by larger positions receive more replies, and prices move more strongly in the direction of large-position commenters. Yet we find no evidence that positions become more predictive of final outcomes, and comment direction does not reliably predict outcomes. The greater engagement and market response therefore do not appear to reflect superior information. The relation between position size and the propensity to comment also strengthens after disclosure; larger-position commenters become more likely to unwind shortly after posting and do so at more favorable prices, consistent with incentives to talk one's book. Overall, the evidence is consistent with position transparency giving traders with larger stakes greater influence over discussion and prices without improving the information available to the market.

detail.abstract: How can we trust the hundreds of return predictors agents can find? We build an autonomous agentic system that searches for return predictors in arbitrary datasets. The system adheres to the scientific method by proposing an economic mechanism, constructing signals, and committing to hypotheses with a full set of test specifications before seeing any returns. In sample, it tests each hypothesis on the median t-statistic across its specifications, with a p-value from a joint block bootstrap of all the specifications, and each hypothesis that passes receives exactly one test on the out-of-sample half. We also apply multiple hypothesis testing corrections to the out-of-sample tests, with both a Holm correction across concurrent tests and an e-value budget that charges each test against all earlier ones. We test the system on H-1B and green card filings from the U.S. Department of Labor, compiled into a point-in-time dataset. The system generates 98 hypotheses with 23,910 specifications in total, and only 11 of the 98 hypotheses survive in sample. Of the 7 out-of-sample tests that the corrections count, 2 survive the Holm correction, and none survives the e-value budget.

detail.abstract: Conventional open-economy macroeconomic models presume unified currency clearing, transparent price discovery, and fully visible capital accounts. In landlocked transition economies across Central Asia-most prominently illustrated by Uzbekistan's post-reform structural evolution (IMF, 2025)-administrative capital controls, historical banking sector dualism, and foreign exchange rationing give rise to persistent parallel market premia. This paper introduces and formalizes a contemporary theoretical construct: The Shadow Elasticity of Capital ($\eta_s$), defined as the marginal responsiveness of unrecorded cross-border capital leakage to high-frequency fluctuations in the parallel market exchange rate premium ($\Phi_t$). Utilizing high-frequency daily informal market pricing data from Tashkent, Samarkand, and key regional trade corridors alongside quarterly Balance of Payments (BoP) statistics spanning 2017-2026, the paper establishes three core empirical findings: 1. Parallel market currency premia act as a statistically significant Granger-causal leading indicator for Balance of Payments Net Errors and Omissions (NEO), anticipating unrecorded capital flight by one to two quarters ($p < 0.001$). 2. When the shadow elasticity threshold exceeds unity ($\eta_s > 1$), central bank policy rate hikes intended to defend official foreign reserves induce a perverse monetary transmission outcome, accelerating formal deposit withdrawal and shifting domestic cash liquidity into informal shadow channels. 3. A newly formulated Informal Financial Stress Index (IFSI) supplies monetary authorities with a daily early-warning indicator to detect systemic liquidity drains prior to official reserve depletion.

detail.abstract: Many firms that run A/B tests struggle with low statistical power, increasing the risk that launch decisions are driven by noise rather than true impact. We argue that in decentralized organizations, low power can reflect misaligned incentives: product teams choose what and how to test on a customer-facing experience to maximize their private reward, while the experience owner sets evaluation rules and launch criteria to optimize the experience. We formalize this interaction via a principal-agent model and show that evaluating tests using raw impact estimates creates a reward to sampling noise. Correctly calibrated posterior-mean evaluation removes this reward and creates a local incentive to reallocate toward fewer, more precise tests of more ambitious ideas. Using data on A/B tests run at Amazon, we document patterns consistent with these model predictions. After an Amazon experience shifted to posterior-mean-based evaluation in 2024, test volume declined while both precision and the dispersion of true impacts increased, more than doubling signal-to-noise ratios. Our results highlight that A/B testing methodologies can shape not only measurement and launch decisions, but which tests are pursued in the first place.

detail.abstract: Does adding stocks to an index genuinely diversify it, or does it merely add securities exposed to the same market forces? This paper separates two components of index diversification: market dominance, the extent to which constituents move together, and residual breadth, the effective number of return dimensions remaining beyond the market factor. An application to two German indices shows that diversification beyond the market factor is persistently below a comparable-market benchmark and varies substantially over time. For the leading blue-chip index, effective residual breadth is typically 22% below its matched benchmark, equivalent to about five fewer effective residual dimensions. A conventional measure can therefore stay stable, or even improve, while the underlying opportunity set narrows, and adding constituents need not widen it. The framework helps index designers, asset allocators and risk managers assess whether an index provides meaningful diversification.

detail.abstract: This essay is a postscript. Following up on my earlier article criticizing the NCAA’s durational eligibility rules pre-2026, this essay describes the new rules the NCAA adopted in June 2026. Those new rules replaced the rules I critiqued in my previous article. The new rules established the “five-for-five” standard: an age-based policy that permits students five years of NCAA eligibility beginning at age nineteen. Litigation challenging the new rules ensued after their passage. The United States Senate also passed the Protect College Sports Act of 2026 addressing similar subject matter and imposing the same standards. In this postscript, I argue that these solutions continue to fall short. I argue that the NCAA should make room for students who are not otherwise qualified to compete under the new standards. Doing so honors the NCAA’s core mission: student participation in institution-affiliated athletics. Since the NCAA continues to impose durational limits in relation to its existing divisions, I propose a novel solution. The NCAA should found a new NCAA division for those students who do not otherwise meet durational eligibility qualifications. Call it NCAA Division X. Our colleges and universities play host to tens of thousands of graduate and professional students who exceed the NCAA durational limits. Among other things, this postscript argues that if the NCAA can make room for Division III athletes, the NCAA should make room for those among the graduate and professional students who can still be student-athletes. It offers NCAA Division X as a way to do that.

detail.abstract: Uzbekistan input-output (I-O) tables in their available version (2021) pose a number of analytical difficulties, including the presence of imports not allocated horizontally across the industries. This may seriously bias the information on technical coefficients, so much so that full Leontieff price models developed on the basis of the I-O matrix become untenable in their findings. Nonetheless, the structural analysis of I-O tables is still possible at a partial, first-pass or n-pass, mode, including for the price models. It can be done sequentially using the proposed algorithm that can be directly implemented in IOTs' Excel spreadsheets. The proposed partial method works directly with the observed intermediate-consumption matrix rather than requiring an inversion of a potentially problematic technical-coefficient matrix. It is also flexible in specifying particular shares for cost passthroughs. The method is illustrated by examining a 35% increase in social security contributions, corresponding to the estimated adjustment required to eliminate the financing gap in Uzbekistan's pay-as-you-go pension system. Assuming full cost pass-through, the estimated mean first-pass price increase across 136 industries is 1.02%, with most industries experiencing increases below 1%. However, the effects are expected to be substantially higher in certain service industries, including social services, education, medical services, and research and development.

detail.abstract: The asset-location literature tells a household to shelter its tax-inefficient assets and keep its tax-efficient ones in the taxable account, and derives that rule for assets that pay interest, dividends and capital gains. Advisers run stranger sleeves. A direct-indexing sleeve manufactures net capital losses. A tax-aware long-short sleeve manufactures far more of them, and no retirement account can hold it. A put-write sleeve earns ordinary interest on its collateral and short-term gains on its premiums. A factor sleeve realizes gains through turnover. We write the location problem for these four sleeves across a taxable account, a traditional IRA and a Roth as a convex piecewise-linear tax cost whose kink is where the taxable account's short-term losses and gains net to zero, and solve it. Once we measure balances after tax the IRA and the Roth are one account, so the problem reduces to what sits in the taxable account. The marginal cost of a sleeve there is its character cost plus a regime-dependent price on its net short-term flow, and a harvested loss can never be worth less than the recapture it creates, which bounds that price from below. Under that bound the ranking is the same in every regime and for every household we consider: long-short, direct indexing, factor tilt, put-write. The textbook order survives, and a 20-year simulation and an exhaustive grid agree it is the optimum. What the model changes is the sizing decision behind the order. With no outside gains a household running direct indexing and long-short holds more losses than it can use, and the long-short sleeve pays only through pre-tax alpha; with outside short-term gains its tax benefit is about 184 basis points per dollar of wealth shifted into it, up to a matched-book size with a closed form. Location is worth 12 to 41 basis points a year over a pro-rata mirror and 16 to 27 over the growth-to-Roth heuristic; the simulation puts the gaps at 19 to 32 and 33 to 40.

detail.abstract: Malaria is a huge public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, but it is not clear to what extent national income, health expenditure and access to sanitation reduce the burden of malaria. In this study, we analyze these relationships using a balanced panel of 31 sub-Saharan African countries during the period 2000–2023 ($N = 744$ country-years). To explore the dispersion of the count data and cross-sectional associations, pooled Poisson and Negative Binomial models were estimated, and then a Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) Negative Binomial model was employed to isolate within-country relationships. Potential endogeneity was checked using a Two-Stage Residual Inclusion (2SRI) control-function approach with a lagged trade-weighted commodity price index . The pooled Poisson model showed extreme overdispersion (Pearson dispersion ratio $\approx 1.85 \times 10^{6}$), in favor of the Negative Binomial specification ($\hat{\alpha} = 0.362$). In the pooled Negative Binomial model, malaria burden was positively associated with GDP per capita ($\text{IRR} = 4.889, p < 0.0001$). However, this association disappeared after controlling for country and year fixed effects ($\text{LR }\chi^2 = 1218.6, p < 0.0001$), with the TWFE model yielding a non-significant protective within-country GDP association ($\text{IRR} = 0.671, p = 0.6798$). Health expenditure (IRR=1.048, p=0.7144) and sanitation access (IRR=0.927, p=0.6919) were also not significant under TWFE. The proposed commodity-price instrument was weakly relevant under fixed effects ($F=0.0758$), causing serious variance propagation in the 2SRI control-function model ($\beta_{\hat{v}}=6.8548,p=0.9392$).These results suggest that the positive relationships between pooled GDP and malaria are confounded by cross-sectional scale, rather than by economic drivers within countries. From a methodological point of view, the results indicate the relevance of controlling for overdispersion and structural country heterogeneity in macro-health models. From a policy standpoint, targeted, malaria-specific interventions and investments in the health system cannot be substituted by overall economic growth.

title: Fiscal integration as a Pareto improvement

detail.title: Fiscal integration as a Pareto improvement

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: Fiscal integration in a currency union is generally understood as a transfer from fiscally strong to fiscally weak countries. I show that this changes when common debt is paired with a non-defaultable common tax, even if national debt remains defaultable. The risky country gains from intertemporal trade: it receives a grant financed by a perpetual obligation it discounts more heavily than lenders do. The cost to the safe member is second-order and the tax removes it by insuring imperfectly correlated cycles rather than transferring resources in expectation. The calibration delivers a narrow Pareto-improving region: the tax that eliminates the risky country’s perverse incentive to default is negligible, while the tax that compensates the safe country is an order of magnitude larger. Joint spending on a public good expands the region and reverses that ordering: the safe country gains even before the common budget balances.

detail.abstract: Rice is the staple food for more than half of the world's population, with global production exceeding 800 million tonnes annually. Yet rice yield is severely threatened by leaf diseases, including bacterial blight, blast, brown spot, and tungro, which collectively cause annual losses of up to 41%. Unlike image-level classification, which assigns a single disease label to the entire image but provides no spatial information about lesion location or extent, semantic segmentation delivers pixel-level localization of diseased tissue, enabling accurate severity assessment and targeted precision spraying. However, publicly available pixel-annotated datasets enabling semantic segmentation remain extremely scarce. This paper makes three principal contributions. First, we release the first large-scale, publicly available pixel-level annotated segmentation dataset for four-class rice leaf disease, comprising 5,932 manually annotated images, available on Mendeley Data. Second, we provide a systematic benchmark of more than 20 segmentation configurations, combining 8 modern segmentation architectures (UNet++, DeepLabV3+, FPN, PSPNet, MAnet, PAN, LinkNet, SegFormer) with 13 ImageNet-pretrained encoder backbones (ResNet34, EfficientNet-B0 to B7, DenseNet121, DenseNet201, Xception, VGG19, ResNeXt50), across multiple training scales. The best configuration, UNet++ with an EfficientNet-B4 backbone trained on the full 5,932-image dataset, achieved a Dice coefficient of 93.47% and an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 87.82%, outperforming all prior methods covering the same four disease classes on publicly available data (best comparable result: Dice 80.3%, MIoU 83.1%). Third, we extended an existing Android application with a new on-device segmentation module using PyTorch Mobile, enabling offline field deployment. Our annotated dataset, benchmark, and mobile module form a complete and reproducible pipeline for rice leaf disease analysis.

detail.abstract: Asserting superior expertise, Presidents have long demanded deference in recognizing national security threats. Courts have generally agreed and acceded. But what if "national security" is not an expert subject to be discovered, but instead a manifestation of community values and fears-an act of communal self-definition? Drawing on history and theory, this article argues that the political nature of national security claims has been fundamentally miscast. Understood as matters of self-determination, claims to national security require democratic ratification. Courts should thus approach national security claims not with the deference owed to expert factual determinations but with the scrutiny appropriate to assertions of national identity and communal values. They should function as democracy-forcing institutions, demanding evidence that securitizing moves have been democratically and representatively ratified before accepting them as justifications for exceptional government action.

detail.abstract: We consider how corporate disclosure affects the board's ability to learn from stock prices. The stock price aggregates investors' assessment of the firm's project and their interpretation of its disclosed performance. The board knows realized performance but not how it is interpreted by investors. With an intermediate level of disclosure, investors' interpretation error affects the stock price, whereas it is nonexistent with full disclosure and irrelevant with no disclosure. This error makes it harder for the board to learn investors' assessment of the firm's project from the stock price: better disclosure improves investors' information but can worsen the board's. Thus, intermediate levels of disclosure are dominated, and minimum disclosure requirements can induce full disclosure. With noisy stock prices, this over-compliance is concentrated among firms with the least noisy stock prices. Board monitoring can increase with the level of disclosure.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the Lutey Value/Growth CAN SLIM approach as a systematic framework that combines growth-oriented stock selection with technical confirmation and portfolio risk management. The central proposition is that fundamental and momentum-based selection can be supplemented by price-volume signals and disciplined portfolio rules to seek long-run growth while limiting severe peak-to-trough losses. Three Portfolio123 backtest screenshots supplied by the author report results against the Russell 1000, S&P 500, and Dow Jones Industrial Average over a displayed period beginning 2 January 1999 and ending 13 October 2026. In the Russell 1000 comparison, the strategy reports a 10.38% annualized return, a 0.75 Sharpe ratio, and a maximum drawdown of-21.81%, versus 8.77%, 0.48, and-55.38% for the benchmark. In the S&P 500 comparison, the corresponding reported values are 10.22%, 0.66, and-30.24%, versus 8.73%, 0.48, and-55.19%. These platform-reported figures are promising but not independently replicated; the screenshots show zero slippage and carry costs, and the strategy configurations differ. The paper situates the approach within research on CAN SLIM, momentum, technical analysis, and market efficiency, and proposes tests needed to establish whether the results persist out of sample after realistic costs and controls for factor exposure, universe construction, and selection bias.

detail.abstract: As U.S. Treasury issuance expands and foreign official demand becomes less reliable, attention has turned to the next marginal buyers of government debt. Although still small relative to the overall Treasury market, dollar-backed stablecoin reserves have grown rapidly and are concentrated in short-term U.S. Treasury securities, making them a potential marginal source of front-end Treasury demand. This paper examines whether stablecoin issuance has become a price-relevant source of demand for U.S. Treasury securities and whether these effects are concentrated at short-duration maturities.Using daily data from 2021 to 2026, distributed-lag regressions show that stablecoin inflows are associated with statistically significant declines in short-term Treasury yields. Across specifications, cumulative stablecoin issuance reduces the 3-month Treasury yield by approximately 1 basis point per $1 billion in net inflows. These effects are concentrated at the front end of the yield curve and dissipate past one year.The stability of this relationship is then evaluated across alternative lag structures, aggregation windows, sample periods, and maturities, with results remaining economically and statistically consistent across model specifications. Impulse responses from a reduced-form vector autoregression further indicate that a one standard-deviation stablecoin flow shock (approximately $1.27 billion) leads to a decline of roughly 3 basis points in the 3-month Treasury yield after five weeks. Taken together, these findings suggest that stablecoin inflows represent a price-relevant source of demand for short-term safe assets and exerts persistent downward pressure on short-term Treasury yields with effects dissipating past the one year.

detail.abstract:
• Context & Objective: The Republic of Uzbekistan is currently in the decisive stages of multilateral and bilateral negotiations to achieve full accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO) by 2026. This study operationalizes classical foreign trade doctrines-specifically Adam Smith's theory of absolute advantage (1776) and David Ricardo's law of comparative advantage (1817)-to quantitatively evaluate the evolution of Uzbekistan's export competitiveness across the 2019-2024 reform cycle and empirically model the sectoral export effects of post-accession tariff liberalizations. • Methodology: Bridging classical foundations with empirical trade econometrics, we construct a calibrated 6-year panel dataset (2019-2024) utilizing verified bilateral and multilateral data from UN Comtrade, the International Trade Centre (ITC Trade Map), and the State Statistics Agency of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Methodologically, we calculate Bela Balassa's Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA) index, the symmetric Normalized Revealed Comparative Advantage (NRCA), and the Hirschman-Herfindahl Index (HHI) of export concentration. Furthermore, an Armington partial equilibrium tariff elasticity simulation model is deployed to project sectoral export responses following foreign tariff reductions under Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) disciplines.
Empirical Findings: The empirical results establish that Uzbekistan possesses pronounced revealed comparative advantages in textiles and finished apparel (RCA = 3.39; NRCA = +0.544) and non ferrous copper metallurgy (RCA = 7.03; NRCA = +0.751). Concurrently, the agro-food sector successfully crossed the parity threshold from comparative disadvantage in 2019 (RCA = 0.82) to revealed advantage in 2024 (RCA = 1.01). Partial equilibrium simulation demonstrates that a post accession tariff reduction (average \Delta \tau = -7.5\%) yields an incremental export surge of +13.9\% in textiles (+\478.7 million) and +10.9\% in agro-food (+\237.1 million), delivering an aggregate annual export dividend exceeding \$923.5 million.
Policy Implications: Relying strictly on raw primary factor endowments exposes the economy to the classical Prebisch-Singer deteriorating terms-of-trade trap. To maximize the societal welfare gains of WTO integration, national industrial policy must transition from "natural factor endowments" to "acquired technological sophistication" by incentivizing deep domestic processing of copper cathodes into high-precision electronics and certifying agro-food exporters under international Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) protocols.

detail.abstract: Experimental reactor datasets are small and strongly correlated, so random data splitting can overstate the predictive skill of empirical models. Six standard machine learning surrogates, a time-only reference model and an Arrhenius first-order cumulative-yield model were benchmarked on 114 conversion measurements of H18-DBT dehydrogenation in a microchannel plate reactor (260-320 °C), using random, leave-onetemperature-out (LOTO) and leave-one-run-out validation. Random splitting gave R2 of 0.94-0.96 for most surrogates, but under LOTO the mean R2 of five of the six fell to 0.13-0.43 (random forest: 0.92). The kinetic model retained R2 = 0.94 and had lower errors than the time-only reference at both extrapolated temperatures, providing a physically constrained basis for extrapolation. The apparent activation energy (about 18 kJ/mol) is a lumped, weakly constrained quantity, and run-to-run scatter at 290 °C limits attainable accuracy. Condition-level validation is therefore essential for small reactor datasets.

detail.abstract:
Machine-operated production and research may eventually alter not only the quantity of present output but also the productive services that subsequent systems can reproduce. Existing economic models address capital reproduction, endogenous innovation, production networks and automated research feedback; formal methods address stochastic viability and multiobjective certificates. This paper contributes a domain-specific intergenerational evidence framework that connects those established mechanisms for a distinct measurement task: deciding whether a joint configuration of services can be delivered and renewed across at least two production generations under a single admissible, observation-adapted policy. The framework separates one-time output, physical capital renewal, independently qualified scientific methods, organizational execution rights and economic valuation. It specifies time-indexed energy, materials, equipment, permission and risk records; supplies two elementary counterexamples showing why separate feasible services and coarse current-output accounts cannot certify joint renewal; and illustrates a two-renewal synthetic schedule with explicit falsification cases. A five-stage investment example distinguishes serial conditional probabilities from latent marginal probabilities and shows that unknown dependence can reverse both certification and investment decisions. A fully informed Bellman benchmark reproduces the same optimal policy, ruling out any claim of intrinsic optimization superiority. The paper’s distinct output is therefore a transparent cross-domain measurement contract, not a new growth theorem, stochastic-control algorithm or empirical proof of autonomous industrial reproduction. It specifies an equal-information, full-cost evaluation that could establish—or reject—the protocol’s practical value. The result is a bounded foundation for cumulative economic investigation of physically and scientifically recursive production.

detail.abstract: Agreement and no-speculation can survive systematic misinterpretation of evidence. On a finite state space, actual signals and their interpreted meanings form two matched partitions. Non-deludedness requires their encodings to agree pointwise; mass balance requires agreement in distribution. Mass balance restores partitional common belief and an Aumann-style agreement theorem despite individual failures of truth and introspection. The ordinary informationpartition theorem is a special case. Once the interpretation rules admit a full-support balancing measure, agreement and the stated no-speculation conclusion are robust to changes in the shared conditioning measure. More generally, a sharp bound controls disagreement by the balance defect relative to the probability of the common-belief region. We also study symmetric higher-order ignorance: under partition range, global KU requires at least five states for nontriviality, while an inclusion-antichain range rules out Boolean closure of awareness. A contracting game links these interpretation errors to strict speculative trade and identifies a second-order belief obstruction to commonly believed execution. All constructions use ordinary events and probability measures on one state space.

detail.abstract: The renewed incidence of military coups has exposed a serious contradiction in Africa's governance and security project. The African Union has developed a dense legal framework against unconstitutional changes of government and has embedded preventive diplomacy, early warning and peace financing within the African Peace and Security Architecture. Yet the sequence of takeovers in Mali, Chad, Guinea, Sudan, Burkina Faso, Niger and Gabon demonstrated that a prohibition regime, by itself, did not reliably prevent political rupture. This paper assessed how governance deficits, weak early action, constrained financing and uneven AU REC coordination interacted to produce that outcome and what this meant for Agenda 2063. It used a qualitative comparative design, combining documentary analysis of African Union and REC instruments, official communiques, budget and financing records, conflict and governance datasets, and published perception evidence. The study treated the 2020 to 2023 coup cycle as an empirical stress test and traced its effects through 2026. It found that the central weakness was not an absence of warning or norms, but a failure to convert warning into preventive political action before institutional legitimacy had collapsed. Sanctions and suspension created costs after a takeover but did not correct the governance conditions that made military intervention publicly tolerable. The AU Peace Fund improved African ownership, but incomplete implementation of the 0.2 per cent levy and the continuing gap between preventive needs and available flexible resources constrained the preventive pillar. The paper argued for an AU REC compact that links governance risk assessment to time bound preventive diplomacy, protected financing and nationally owned reform benchmarks. It concluded that Agenda 2063 will be protected less by a stronger rhetoric of zero tolerance than by institutions able to act on credible warnings before citizens and soldiers conclude that constitutional politics has ceased to offer remedy.

detail.abstract: Machine learning classifiers deployed in financial transaction streams face severe operational challenges, including extreme class imbalance (∼ 0.167 fraud prevalence), costly false positive alarms, and artificial performance inflation caused by duplicate instances spanning training and test splits [1, 8]. In this work, the author presents a modular, four-stage deep learning pipeline designed to systematically clean, analyze, scale, train, and evaluate transaction data without data leakage. By identifying and purging 1,081 duplicate records from a benchmark dataset of 284,807 instances, the author establishes a clean evaluation baseline of 283,726 unique records (283,253 legitimate and 473 fraudulent transactions). Temporal and amount variables are normalized via standard 𝑍-score scaling alongside 28 Principal Component Analysis (PCA) features, followed by a stratified 80 20 train/test split (56,746 held-out test transactions). The author built a four-layer Keras Sequential Deep Neural Network with dropout regularization [14] and optimize the risk decision threshold from the standard 0.50 default to 𝑇 𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑘 = 0.35. Evaluated strictly on unseen test data, the pipeline achieves Precision = 87.18, Recall = 71.58, and an F1-Score = 78.61 for the minority fraud class, while maintaining an exceptional false alarm rate of only 0.0176 (10 false positives out of 56,651 normal cases). Furthermore, the author demonstrates how this offline pipeline acts as an inline behavioral risk scoring engine within adaptive multi-factor and biometric security frameworks [12, 13, 18].

title: From Basic Income to Micro-Power: Governmentality, Care of the Self, and Union of Egoists
affiliations: Kyungpook National University

detail.title: From Basic Income to Micro-Power: Governmentality, Care of the Self, and Union of Egoists

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper constructs an ideal-typical scenario in five conditional links. It asks what follows politically if AI-driven automation reduces the market value of most people's labor to a minimum. The first link is inductive: the wage ceases to connect the majority reliably to the means of life. The central links are genealogical. Because taxation, consent and order depend on the wage relation, the state's conditions of existence come under pressure. A state-led basic income is read as the survival measure of governmental reason, adopted by a quasi-automatic logic and not by normative persuasion. Such an income would also produce an excess of micro-power through identification, data and algorithmic administration. Individuals could respond with the care of the self as counter-conduct, separated from self-enterprise by three criteria: the end of the practice, who judges it, and its reversibility. Where these hold, the products of self-care could acquire value in a counter-state union of egoists, a Stirnerian free market society of self-owners. Support weakens along the chain, and the final stage remains a theoretical construction. The paper offers precisely stated questions, not a forecast.

detail.abstract: Multi-modal machine learning architectures incorporating the integration of EHR and diagnostic medical images have exhibited tremendous predictive performance for acute triage and in-hospital mortality prediction. However, their wide-spread clinical deployment continues to be highly impeded by their black-box behavior. Post-hoc explainability methods (including SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM) often produce explanations that seem plausible, yet do not correspond to the true underlying computation performed by the model - a problemreferred to as the faithfulness-plausibility dilemma. This paper introduces and develops the Cross-Modal Concept Bottleneck Model (XM-CBM), a fundamentally interpretable multi-modal deep learning architecture that ensures reasoning through clinically meaningful concepts. To ensure the faithfulness of explanation, we propose a combined optimization function with a faithfulness penalty and cross-modal concept semantic similarity objective. Benchmarked on 12,847 matched adult ICU admissions from the MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR databases across 5-fold stratified cross-validation, XM-CBM achieves diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.854 ± 0.012, AUPRC 0.593 ± 0.024) comparable to unrestricted late-fusion black-box baselines (AUROC 0.867 ± 0.009). Importantly, the quantitative interpretability auditing shows that the XM-CBM results in a 50.5% decrease in the area under curve for deletion (0.142 vs 0.287), a 20.8% increase in the area under curve for insertion (0.823 vs 0.681), and a 76.2% decrease in the infidelity of explanation (0.034 vs 0.143) while significantly enhancing the adversarial stability of explanations. This proves that high diagnostic accuracy and mathematical explanation faithfulness are not mutually exclusive in high-stakes clinical decision support

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as substitutes for expert judgment in the production of democratic information goods, raising question about their reliability and alignment. This paper examines whether LLMs can replicate one specific form of political expertise: the ideological classification of policy statements. Using 74 statements from the Belgian Voting Aid Application (VAA), we compare classifications produced by four leading LLMs with benchmark labels assigned by expert political scientists. We find that LLMs classify clearly ideological statements with impressive accuracy, achieving scores exceeding 97% accuracy. However, all tested models struggle with statements that experts classify as neutral, displaying a systematic tendency to assign ideological meaning to statements that human coders regard as non-ideological. We refer to this pattern as over-ideologization. The findings suggest that LLMs can substantially reduce the costs of production of information goods critical to the democratic process. However, dealing with ambiguity maybe a challenge yet to overcome.

detail.abstract: We show that active funds, classified as fixed income funds managed by asset managers, selectively increase their holdings in downgraded bonds that subsequently earn positive abnormal returns and receive rating upgrades. Active funds are more likely to increase holdings of downgraded bonds when (i) the downgrade is predictable, (ii) sell-side bond analyst recommendations are favorable, (iii) collateralized loan obligations (CLOs) acquire the issuing firms' loans, and (iv) issuer management provides revenue or EBITDA guidance. The evidence suggests that active funds act as informed liquidity providers in the corporate bond market, able to identify downgraded bonds whose credit subsequently recovers.

title: Vacancy Chains as Strategy: Inter-Organization Mobility of Political Elites in Reform China
affiliations: University of Chicago and Independent

detail.title: Vacancy Chains as Strategy: Inter-Organization Mobility of Political Elites in Reform China
detail.abstract: Questions of career advancement and success have long occupied scholars of the Chinese state. Most work on political mobility in China views mobility from the perspective of the individual. It imagines a pool of officials who are at risk of moving up a status hierarchy of positions and the goal is to explain why some succeed and others fail. We develop a complementary account that views mobility not from the perspective of the individual, but from the perspective of the organization trying to fill positions. Such a perspective does more justice to the bureaucratic nature of the Chinese party-state in which hiring is centrally coordinated by high-level elites in the CCP. Focusing on the organization directs our attention to the strategies behind personnel management. We argue that those strategies can be studied through an analysis of vacancy chains. Drawing on a novel dataset of more than 2,500 inter-organizational transfers derived from the CVs of more than 4,000 political elites included in the Chinese Political Elite Database, we show that between 1977 and 2012 elites whose transfers are embedded in long vacancy chains are more successful than those whose transfers occur in isolation. In addition, we demonstrate that this career boost occurs after their involvement in vacancy chains and that it is stronger for younger elites than for older ones. We contend that these findings are the result of a strategy of organizational sponsorship pursued by the CCP that results from efforts to integrate the increasingly decentralized Chinese state.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how higher-education policy impacts gender inequality when students decide both college attendance and major selection. We develop a quantitative life-cycle model incorporating endogenous college enrollment, college major, saving, and fertility. Policies can shift Gender Income Gap and Gender Welfare Gap in opposite directions by altering student sorting across fields. Universal free tuition may widen the income gap while narrowing the welfare gap. Conversely, gender-based affirmative action has minimal effect on earnings gaps but can worsen welfare disparities. Evaluating policy solely through earnings gaps may be misleading when there exists gender heterogeneity by major.

detail.abstract: When a business is valued in two currencies, the local-currency and foreign-currency discounted cash flow values can be the same. That agreement is easily read as support for the terminal growth rate. This paper tests the reading on a constructed ringgit and US dollar valuation, using a known translation identity and twelve diagnostic cases. The cases separate mechanical error from shared economic assumptions, and both of those from problems of interpretation and data provenance. Inputs available at the valuation date are kept apart from data published later. Growth left untranslated opens a gap of 7.5 per cent, and an inverted exchange-rate path opens one of 5.9 per cent. An error made in both currencies, however, reconciles exactly, and so do two offsetting errors confined to a single currency. Agreement therefore establishes neither correct mechanics nor a defensible growth rate. On matched IMF terminal inflation proxies, the constructed path implies a real exchange-rate wedge of 0.47 per cent a year. Other proxies reverse the sign, so the wedge is a conditional reading of the path rather than a forecast of the currency. Reconciliation tests consistency and nothing more. Growth has to be supported on its own terms: by the reinvestment it requires, the return that investment earns, evidence from the firm and its industry, and dated macroeconomic context. The parity algebra is already known, and what the paper adds is the classification of the diagnostic cases and a review sequence that can be tested. The model assumes deterministic projections, zero covariance between currency and cash flows, all-equity financing and flat base yields. It uses no sample of practitioner behaviour, and the review sequence itself has not been tested. A technical appendix carries the proofs and the workings behind every table.

detail.abstract: Corruption opportunities attract people who would exploit them and repel people who anticipate the cost of resisting them. I study both margins in a model of occupational choice with self-control costs. Three results stand out. First, when temptation is strong, small corruption rents can shrink the pool of entrants. Second, the public sector can lose integrity while it shrinks, so a stable or falling headcount can conceal a deteriorating workforce. Third, at equal net corrupt surplus, removing corruption opportunities yields weakly lower corruption than deferred sanctions, both at a given wage and with a fixed number of posts. When rents rise with the share of corrupt incumbents, the ranking carries over to steady states, and prevention can eliminate a high-corruption equilibrium that an equivalent sanction preserves.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether bank monitoring reduces firms' stock price crash risk by limiting managers' incentives to withhold information. We exploit the default of the Baoshang Bank in 2019 in China as an exogenous shock that weakened expectations of banks' implicit government guarantees (IGGs) and enhanced bank monitoring. We define firms that borrow from systematically unimportant banks (SUBs) as treatment and firms that borrow from systematically important banks (SIBs) as control. We find that, following the default, treatment firms experienced significantly lower crash risk than control firms. The results are robust after pre-trend tests, placebo tests, and multiple tests to address sample selection bias, suggesting that the findings are likely causal. Consistent with the assumption that the default enhances bank monitoring, following the default, SUBs are associated with higher asset quality but no difference in liability structures than SIBs. Also, the negative treatment effect on stock price crash risk is more pronounced in areas where banks have less incentives to monitor ex ante. Consistent with the assumption that the default weakens borrowers' incentives to withhold information, following the default, treatment firms are associated with higher information quality and more timely information disclosure. We also find a stronger negative treatment effect when firms are more informationally opaque, with higher ownership concentration, or with higher demand for external finance, especially finance from SUBs. The findings provide causal evidence that bank monitoring reduces borrower crash risk by improving borrower disclosure quality and mitigating borrowers' incentives to withhold information.

detail.abstract: Account-to-account payment between institutions requires resolving a human-readable identifier-a phone number, an alias, a handle-to an account. Card schemes never needed the capability, and every account-to-account scheme that reached a physical checkout from elsewhere has had to build it. This paper compares three architectures that answer the question differently: Brazil, where a single directory at the central bank holds over one billion keys; India, where resolution splits by identifier type, with nationally minted identifiers held centrally and provider-issued handles resolved by their issuer; and the Bank for International Settlements' Nexus design, which declines to operate a directory at all on the grounds that it does not own the systems it interlinks. It then sets out what European schemes do today-each resolving only its own members, with bilateral interoperability between them-and examines the two European attempts at a shared directory, one central and one federated, both free and neither adopted. The paper argues against centralising the European address layer. The evidence indicates that the obstacle was never architecture, cost or privacy engineering, but ownership: a central directory asks every national scheme to surrender the customer relationship it exists to defend. Centralising the institution is not the same as centralising the data.

title: Coerced Consent and the Limits of Voluntary Exchange in Contract Law

detail.abstract: Economists and contract theorists appeal to "voluntary exchange" as the normative foundation of enforceable agreements, yet the concept does far less work than it appears. If "voluntary" means rational and informed choice, it captures transactions no legal system would enforce; if it means exchanges that promote efficiency or fairness, it collapses into tautology. This Article argues that the real analytical work is done by the distinction between two configurations of coercive pressure: cases in which the counterparty engineers the conditions of necessity and cases in which it merely exploits a pre-existing one. Drawing on Italian, French, German, and United States law, the Article shows that this distinction predicts, with notable regularity, both when consent is treated as defective and which remedy follows. Engineered necessity tends to support categorical invalidity and disgorgement; exploited necessity more often calls for price-conditioned intervention such as judicial adjustment of consideration or rescission coupled with fair compensation. The Article engages with leading philosophical accounts of coercion, from Nozick to Fried, and argues that they remain incomplete because they fail to incorporate credible threats. The economic analysis connects these remedial patterns to problems of deterrence, chilling effects, and holdup , explaining why legal systems converge on calibrated review despite divergent doctrinal categories. A central finding is that efficiency and fairness, often assumed to stand in tension, point in the same direction. Both support invalidity where necessity is engineered and calibrated intervention where it is exploited. The framework carries concrete implications for U.S. unconscionability, duress, and contract modification.

detail.abstract: Introduction: Routine computed tomography (CT) provides readily interpretable information on colorectal cancer (CRC), however, whether conventional CT characteristics combined with tumor location can characterize metastatic presentation remains unclear.,Methods: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 115 adults with CRC. Clinical, anatomical, CT, staging, and histopathological data were collected. Stage IV disease was compared with stages II–III disease. A parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model incorporating the maximum lesion dimension, left-sided tumor location, and CT-detected bowel wall thickening was evaluated using ROC analysis, calibration, and bootstrap internal validation.,Results: Stage was classifiable in 112 patients, including 31 (27.7%) with Stage IV disease. Left-sided location was independently associated with lower odds of Stage IV presentation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.186, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.056–0.616; p = 0.006), while bowel-wall thickening showed a possible association with increased odds (aOR = 2.610, 95% CI: 0.985–6.914; p = 0.054). The model achieved an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.738 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.713. Stage IV frequency differed by tumor location (p = 0.015), being highest in rectal/rectosigmoid tumors (42.9%).,Conclusions: Primary tumor location is an important component of the routine CT phenotype associated with metastatic CRC. Simple, interpretable CT characteristics showed moderate discriminatory ability, supporting further evaluations in larger, externally validated cohorts.

detail.abstract: U.S. equity returns respond to abnormal temperature variability, a distinct and economically consequential dimension of temperature exposure not subsumed by extreme temperatures or heatwave persistence. Using state-level shocks assigned to firms with geographically concentrated operations, we find that low-exposure firms contemporaneously outperform high-exposure firms by 4.4\% per year. Elevated variability is associated with lower firm revenues and profits, reduced household spending, and fewer hours worked. Yet the firm-level cash-flow implications of these shocks remain difficult to assess as analyst disagreement rises and subsequent earnings surprises become more negative. Despite this uncertainty, returns adjust primarily as the shock materializes.

detail.abstract: A growing body of legal scholarship, copyright offices and major stakeholders argue that automated in-software private content regulation is critical to quell the ability for AI tools to create copyright infringing works, or AI companies risk being found liable for contributing to the ensuing infringement. This article argues the opposite: the greatest threat to copyright posed by Generative AI systems is widespread privatisation of copyright regulation during creative production, at the expense of copyright's purpose of stimulating innovative production and its critical balancing exceptions. Copyright infringement is an inherently qualitative and often contentious assessment, one which algorithms are ill-equipped to evaluate. The article argues that exposing AI companies to further liability would undermine copyright's crucial balancing act, functionally driving over-regulation and thereby suppressing copyright's critical exceptions from an entire mode of creative production. Further, it would incentivise unnecessary media partnerships that risk undermining copyright's purpose to stimulate innovative production, instead establishing ecosystems wherein legacy rightsholders need no longer be productive to extract rent from the next generation of producers, solely for the service of allowing them to produce. If GenAI tools end up forming a large part of creative productive ecosystems, then copyright regulation could cede relevance to private interests over a staggering percentage of 21 st century creativity-all in avoidance of infringement that is already well-regulated. The article concludes that this level of intervention at the point of production would truly be unprecedented, surrendering copyright to the control of a crooked brush.

detail.abstract: This paper reports the association between Neuroticism and risk aversion in a five-item hypothetical lottery task administered to an Indian convenience sample (158 responses; N = 157 after applying the completeness rule). Neuroticism correlated with the Risk Aversion Index at r = .303, 95% CI [.154, .439], an estimate stable across subgroup and item-content specifications. Intolerance of Uncertainty correlated at r = .295, statistically indistinguishable from Neuroticism, and the two scales share 63% of the variance they jointly explain; entered together, only Neuroticism retains a significant coefficient, but the two unique components are close in magnitude. Item-level Neuroticism correlations peak at the 60% item (r = .361) and are weakest at the 90% item (r = .070), but the correlation for near-indifference items does not differ significantly from that for expected-value-dominant items (r_hard = .310 vs r_easy = .212; Fisher z = 0.92, p = .356). A residual Neuroticism effect on the 60% item survives control for the 50% item (b = 0.158, SE = 0.036, p < .001), which locates the item-level signal at one question rather than along a difficulty gradient. Because choices were hypothetical, the sample is a young, educated convenience sample, the item order was fixed and ascending, and the study was not preregistered, these results are descriptive and require preregistered replication under randomized order.

detail.abstract: In December 1986 SFAS 89 made the inflation disclosures of SFAS 33 voluntary, and U.S. financial statements have since been prepared on an unadjusted historical-cost basis. Consumer prices rose 197% between 1986 and 2025. This paper measures where that inflation now sits in the financial statements of U.S. companies. BEA fixed-asset accounts show that current-cost depreciation of the non-financial corporate sector exceeded historical-cost depreciation in every year, by 16% in 2025 and by 5.3 trillion dollars cumulatively since 1986, equivalent on average to 17% of NIPA pre-tax profits. Accelerated tax depreciation offset this gap for tax purposes until the mid-2000s; since 2005, economic depreciation at current cost has exceeded tax depreciation by about 1.0 trillion dollars, implying roughly US$ 324 billion of federal tax on capital consumption. A closed-form replacement ratio driven only by the CPI tracks the BEA series closely, with a mean absolute error of 0.023. Using SEC XBRL filings for 2009-2025, the median equity restatement factor of non-financial companies is 1.52, with a floor of 1.35 that requires no assumption about the age of the opening balance: book equity omits a quarter to a third of the capital formed in the median company. Median debt-to-equity measured in constant dollars falls from 0.48 to 0.31 once equity is restated, and 128 of the 259 companies with book leverage above one drop below it. Firm-level reinvestment depends on the denominator: the median ratio of capital expenditure to depreciation proper was 1.11 in 2025, but against depreciation plus amortization it was 0.73, below one in every year since 2009. Below a price-to-book multiple equal to the restatement factor, the entire premium attributed to intangibles is monetary erosion of the denominator.

detail.abstract: Regulatory requirements can affect economic outcomes by changing the demands placed on scarce resources. We examine this possibility in an audit setting using the Jumpstart Our Business Startups (JOBS) Act, which reduced the regulatory and reporting requirements associated with initial public offerings (IPOs) made by Emerging Growth Companies (EGCs). We find that before the JOBS Act, greater audit office exposure to IPOs that would have qualified as EGCs is associated with lower audit quality for non-IPO clients. After the Act, non-IPO clients in EGC IPO offices experience a differential improvement in audit quality. The post-JOBS improvement is primarily evident when EGC IPOs take advantage of the Act's reduced audited financial statement requirements and is more pronounced when audit offices have less capacity to accommodate IPO-related workloads. Collectively, our findings suggest that regulatory relief affecting one use of scarce audit office resources can affect audit quality for other clients competing for those resources.

detail.abstract: Article 4 of Law 9,249/1995 abolished inflation accounting in Brazil. Between 1996 and 2025 the consumer price index (IPCA) rose 494.9%, yet no mandatory standard recognizes the effect, because the hyperinflation threshold of IAS 29 was never reached. This paper measures where that inflation now sits, using the consolidated standardized financial statements filed with the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) by 739 listed companies from 2010 to 2025 (6,312 firm-years). Rebuilding equity by vintage from the statement of changes in equity, the median restatement factor is 2.57 under the central assumption and 1.79 at a floor that does not age the opening balance; treating the 2010 deemed-cost revaluations as current values moves the median by less than 1%. With firm-specific factors, median debt-to-equity measured in constant currency falls from 0.87 to 0.33, and 54 of the 90 firms with book leverage above one drop below it. Book weights bias the weighted average cost of capital by up to 151 basis points when the cost of equity is taken as given, and falls to a little over half of that when beta is relevered consistently. The median ratio of capital expenditure to depreciation fell from 1.88 in 2010 to 0.87 in 2025, or 1.11 including lease payments, below the 1.24 replacement ratio required for ten-year assets. Historical-cost depreciation in 2025 falls R$ 93.5 billion short of replacement-cost depreciation, on which about R$ 31.8 billion of corporate income taxes would be levied at the statutory rate. Computed on restated equity, the ceiling of the tax benefit of interest on equity would nearly double. Below a price-to-book multiple equal to the restatement factor, the entire premium usually attributed to intangibles is monetary erosion of the denominator. The paper closes with four minimum disclosures for valuation reports.

detail.abstract:
This article places Generative AI (GenAI) in a broader lineage of technological innovations in creative production and ascertains why copyright struggles to accommodate recognition of AI-generated works. Specifically, it considers how current copyright law would render the bulk of GenAI’s most innovative applications as resulting in works that are either unprotected or infringing.


The article develops an explanatory framework for copyright’s increasing tension with the techno-creative innovation that it ostensibly seeks to stimulate, which it conceptualises in five pillars:


1. Lack of protection for innovative new modes of creative expression

2. Prohibition of innovative modes of expression dependent upon reuse of protected expression

3. Vastly more permissive allowance for expressive differentiation based on pre-existing expression if the work is recreated

4. Vulnerability to scale enabled by cheapening cost and labour of creative production

5. Inability to accommodate heightened media fluidity due to reliance on fixation


It exhibits the means by which advances in creative technologies continue to stretch the coherence of copyright through these five pillars, with GenAI intensifying all five to breaking point.


As progressively more socially valuable culture leaks out of copyright’s remit, this article questions the extent to which public copyright frameworks are solely responsible for regulating an increasingly arbitrary quotient of cultural production - with effective governance of the rest migrating towards private infrastructures capable of accommodating contemporary cultural production and dissemination logics. It questions the extent to which this shift of importance to private infrastructures preserves the appearance of doctrinal continuity, maintaining formalistic coherence, while sacrificing the relevance of copyright over substantial portions of contemporary creative production.

detail.abstract: This study provides comprehensive empirical validation and quantitative macro-operational stresstesting for Part II of the International Integrated Clearing and Settlement System (IICSS), an output-pegged Multi-CBDC Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) framework. While theoretical mechanism design establishes the normative feasibility of suppressing ex-nihilo credit expansion and insulating sovereign nations from correspondent clearing frictions, transitioning such architectures to global deployment requires evaluating geopolitical adoption tipping points, papermarket commodity derivative distortions, pre-genesis monetary overhang, and credit diversion risks. Integrating Evolutionary Game Theory (EGT), continuous-time state-space dynamics, and constrained stochastic optimization models, we evaluate the system's operational viability across four core macro-geopolitical vectors. Replicator dynamics simulation confirms that as BRICS+ trade gravity and legacy sanction risks breach critical thresholds, IICSS adoption becomes the sole Globally Evolutionary Stable Strategy (ESS), driving 100% adoption convergence. Empirical evaluation of the Gold Clearance Gateway proves that the Intrinsic Commodity-Technology Index (𝑃 *) isolates benchmark clearing rates from speculative COMEX/LBMA paper leverage (𝜕𝐶𝐵𝑅 𝜕𝐿 𝑝𝑎𝑝𝑒𝑟 = 0). Furthermore, state-space transition modeling validates that locked Tier-2 Transition Bonds are systematically converted into active Tier-1 liquidity strictly in proportion to verified real output growth (Δ𝑌 𝑡 > 0), neutralizing historical monetary overhang without nominal haircuts or postgenesis inflation. Finally, algorithmic Purpose-Bound Debt (PBD) execution bounds capital flight leakage to zero (𝐶𝐹 ≡ 0), channeling 100% of disbursed credit directly into Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF). These quantitative findings confirm that IICSS Part II establishes a resilient, non-speculative operational layer for global monetary sovereignty.

title: Capital accumulation in clean technologies by manufacturing firms with heterogeneous absorptive capacity
